287 +
288 + class ReferralSettings(BaseSettings):
289 +     """Referral programme and internal bonus balance.
290 +
291 +     Percentages and the bonus exchange rate are *configuration*, not business
292 +     data: they are read once on start-up and validated there, exactly like the
293 +     delivery retry policy. Changing them is a deploy, which is deliberate —
294 +     a mistyped reward percent must not be applicable through a web form while
295 +     money is moving.
296 +
297 +     ``enabled`` is a master switch. With it off the shop behaves exactly as it
298 +     did before the feature existed: no referral payload is recognised, no
299 +     discount is applied and no bonus is accrued or spent.
300 +
301 +     There is deliberately no exchange rate here. One bonus is one Telegram
302 +     Star, and a purchase settled in USDT is converted using the *product's own*
303 +     two prices at the moment of the sale — see ``Product.stars_per_usdt``. That
304 +     keeps the shop free of any external price feed, and of any fixed rate that
305 +     would silently go stale.
306 +     """
307 +
308 +     model_config = _settings_config("REFERRAL_")
309 +
310 +     enabled: bool = True
311 +     discount_percent: int = Field(default=10, ge=0, le=MAX_PERCENT)
312 +     """Discount on the invited buyer's first qualifying purchase."""
313 +
314 +     reward_percent: int = Field(default=15, ge=0, le=MAX_PERCENT)
315 +     """Share of every settled purchase credited to the inviter as bonuses."""
316 +
317 +     max_bonus_payment_percent: int = Field(default=50, ge=0, le=MAX_PERCENT)
318 +     """Largest share of a Stars price that bonuses may cover.
319 +
320 +     One bonus is one Telegram Star, so this is read directly off the price: a
321 +     1000 Star product accepts at most 500 bonuses at 50%.
322 +     """
323 +
324 +     preview_directory_url: str | None = None
325 +     """Single hop channel listing the current preview channels.
326 +
327 +     The bot stores no channel ids, no channel usernames and no list: it only
328 +     knows this one URL, so the catalogue of preview channels is managed outside
329 +     the bot and changing it never requires a redeploy. Empty hides the button.
330 +     """
331 +
332 +     @field_validator("preview_directory_url", mode="before")
333 +     @classmethod
334 +     def _blank_url_means_none(cls, value: object) -> object:
335 +         """Treat ``REFERRAL_PREVIEW_DIRECTORY_URL=`` in an env file as unset."""
336 +         if isinstance(value, str) and not value.strip():
337 +             return None
338 +         return value
339 +
340 +     @field_validator("preview_directory_url")
341 +     @classmethod
342 +     def _validate_preview_url(cls, value: str | None) -> str | None:
343 +         if value is None:
344 +             return None
345 +         candidate = value.strip()
346 +         parsed = urlparse(candidate)
347 +         if parsed.scheme not in _PREVIEW_URL_SCHEMES or not parsed.netloc:
348 +             msg = "preview_directory_url must be an absolute http(s) URL"
349 +             raise ValueError(msg)
350 +         return candidate
351 +
352 +     @model_validator(mode="after")
353 +     def _keep_a_price_payable(self) -> Self:
354 +         """A purchase must always leave something to charge.
355 +
356 +         A 100% discount would produce a zero invoice, which the purchases table
357 +         rejects (``amount > 0``) — better to refuse the configuration on
358 +         start-up than to fail inside a checkout.
359 +         """
360 +         if self.discount_percent >= MAX_PERCENT:
361 +             msg = "discount_percent must leave something to charge (< 100)"
362 +             raise ValueError(msg)
363 +         if self.max_bonus_payment_percent >= MAX_PERCENT:
364 +             msg = "max_bonus_payment_percent must leave something to charge (< 100)"
365 +             raise ValueError(msg)
366 +         return self
367 +
368 +
369 + class SecuritySettings(BaseSettings):
370 +     """Admin authentication and browser-facing security policy."""
371 +
372 +     model_config = _settings_config("SECURITY_")
373 +
374 +     jwt_secret: SecretStr
375 +     jwt_algorithm: Literal["HS256", "HS384", "HS512"] = "HS256"
376 +     access_token_ttl_minutes: int = Field(default=15, ge=1, le=1440)
377 +     refresh_token_ttl_days: int = Field(default=14, ge=1, le=90)
378 +     admin_username: str = Field(min_length=3, max_length=64)
379 +     admin_password: SecretStr
380 +     # Credential guessing protection on the admin login endpoint.
381 +     login_rate_limit: int = Field(default=10, ge=1, le=1000)
382 +     login_rate_window_seconds: float = Field(default=300.0, ge=1.0, le=3600.0)
383 +     # The refresh token travels in an httpOnly cookie; Secure is dropped only
384 +     # for plain-HTTP local development.
385 +     cookie_secure: bool = True
386 +     cookie_name: str = "tgshop_refresh"
387 +     # NoDecode keeps pydantic-settings from JSON-decoding the raw env value, so
388 +     # the comma separated form below is parsed by the validator instead.
389 +     cors_origins: Annotated[tuple[str, ...], NoDecode] = ()
390 +
391 +     @field_validator("jwt_secret")
392 +     @classmethod
393 +     def _validate_jwt_secret(cls, value: SecretStr) -> SecretStr:
394 +         if len(value.get_secret_value()) < MIN_JWT_SECRET_LENGTH:
395 +             msg = f"jwt_secret must be at least {MIN_JWT_SECRET_LENGTH} characters long"
396 +             raise ValueError(msg)
397 +         return value
398 +
399 +     @field_validator("admin_password")
400 +     @classmethod
401 +     def _validate_admin_password(cls, value: SecretStr) -> SecretStr:
402 +         if len(value.get_secret_value()) < MIN_ADMIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH:
403 +             msg = f"admin_password must be at least {MIN_ADMIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH} characters long"
404 +             raise ValueError(msg)
405 +         return value
406 +
407 +     @field_validator("cors_origins", mode="before")
408 +     @classmethod
409 +     def _split_origins(cls, value: object) -> object:
410 +         if isinstance(value, str):
411 +             return tuple(origin.strip() for origin in value.split(",") if origin.strip())
412 +         return value

1   + """Composition root.
2   +
3   + Wiring lives here and nowhere else: services receive their collaborators, never
4   + construct them. Both entrypoints (admin API, bot) build one container per
5   + process from the shared infrastructure resources.
6   + """
7   +
8   + from __future__ import annotations
9   +
10  + from dataclasses import dataclass, replace
11  + from datetime import timedelta
12  + from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
13  +
14  + from app.infrastructure.cache.locks import RedisLockManager
15  + from app.infrastructure.cache.rate_limit import RedisRateLimiter
16  + from app.infrastructure.cache.revocation import RedisTokenRevocationStore
17  + from app.infrastructure.db.uow import SqlAlchemyUnitOfWorkFactory
18  + from app.infrastructure.payments.cryptobot import CryptoBotClient
19  + from app.services.auth import AuthService
20  + from app.services.bonuses import BonusService
21  + from app.services.checkout import CheckoutService
22  + from app.services.delivery import DeliveryService
23  + from app.services.products import ProductService
24  + from app.services.purchases import PurchaseService
25  + from app.services.referrals import ReferralService
26  + from app.services.stats import StatsService
27  +
28  + if TYPE_CHECKING:
29  +     from app.core.config import Settings
30  +     from app.core.resources import Resources
31  +     from app.domain.delivery import DeliveryGateway
32  +     from app.domain.notifications import RewardNotifier
33  +     from app.domain.payments import StarsInvoiceSender
34  +
35  +
36  + @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
37  + class Container:
38  +     """Every service the process can use, already wired."""
39  +
40  +     settings: Settings
41  +     uow_factory: SqlAlchemyUnitOfWorkFactory
42  +     locks: RedisLockManager
43  +     rate_limiter: RedisRateLimiter
44  +     crypto_payments: CryptoBotClient
45  +     products: ProductService
46  +     purchases: PurchaseService
47  +     referrals: ReferralService
48  +     bonuses: BonusService
49  +     stats: StatsService
50  +     auth: AuthService
51  +
52  +     @classmethod
53  +     def create(cls, resources: Resources) -> Container:
54  +         """Build the container from the process's infrastructure resources."""
55  +         settings = resources.settings
56  +         uow_factory = SqlAlchemyUnitOfWorkFactory(resources.database)
57  +         locks = RedisLockManager(resources.cache.client, settings.redis)
58  +         # Pricing is built before the purchase service because the purchase
59  +         # service takes it as a collaborator: the discount and the bonus hold
60  +         # have to commit in the same transaction as the purchase row.
61  +         bonuses = BonusService(
62  +             uow_factory=uow_factory,
63  +             locks=locks,
64  +             settings=settings.referral,
65  +         )
66  +         purchases = PurchaseService(
67  +             uow_factory=uow_factory,
68  +             locks=locks,
69  +             invoice_ttl=timedelta(seconds=settings.cryptobot.invoice_ttl_seconds),
70  +             pricing=bonuses,
71  +         )
72  +         return cls(
73  +             settings=settings,
74  +             uow_factory=uow_factory,
75  +             locks=locks,
76  +             rate_limiter=RedisRateLimiter(resources.cache.client),
77  +             crypto_payments=CryptoBotClient(settings.cryptobot),
78  +             products=ProductService(uow_factory=uow_factory, telegram=settings.telegram),
79  +             purchases=purchases,
80  +             referrals=ReferralService(
81  +                 uow_factory=uow_factory,
82  +                 telegram=settings.telegram,
83  +                 settings=settings.referral,
84  +             ),
85  +             bonuses=bonuses,
86  +             stats=StatsService(uow_factory=uow_factory),
87  +             auth=AuthService(
88  +                 settings.security,
89  +                 RedisTokenRevocationStore(resources.cache.client),
90  +             ),
91  +         )
92  +
93  +     def build_checkout(
94  +         self,
95  +         *,
96  +         delivery_gateway: DeliveryGateway,
97  +         stars: StarsInvoiceSender,
98  +         notifier: RewardNotifier | None = None,
99  +     ) -> CheckoutService:
100 +         """Wire checkout to a concrete transport (bot process or admin API)."""
101 +         return CheckoutService(
102 +             purchases=self.purchases,
103 +             delivery=self.build_delivery(delivery_gateway, notifier=notifier),
104 +             stars=stars,
105 +             crypto=self.crypto_payments,
106 +         )
107 +
108 +     def build_delivery(
109 +         self,
110 +         gateway: DeliveryGateway,
111 +         *,
112 +         notifier: RewardNotifier | None = None,
113 +     ) -> DeliveryService:
114 +         """Create the delivery service for a concrete transport.
115 +
116 +         The transport only exists in the bot process, so it is supplied here
117 +         instead of being stored on the container.
118 +         """
119 +         return DeliveryService(
120 +             uow_factory=self.uow_factory,
121 +             purchases=self.purchases,
122 +             gateway=gateway,
123 +             locks=self.locks,
124 +             settings=self.settings.delivery,
125 +             sale_completion=self.build_bonuses(notifier=notifier),
126 +         )
127 +
128 +     def build_bonuses(self, *, notifier: RewardNotifier | None = None) -> BonusService:
129 +         """The bonus service, optionally able to tell an inviter they earned.
130 +
131 +         The notifier lives in the bot process only, so the container keeps a
132 +         transport-free instance and hands out a notifying one on request.
133 +         """
134 +         if notifier is None:
135 +             return self.bonuses
136 +         return replace(self.bonuses, notifier=notifier)

1  + """Structured logging setup.
2  +
3  + A single stdout stream carries every log record: JSON in production (ready for
4  + Loki/ELK ingestion) and colourised key-value output during local development.
5  + Standard library loggers used by uvicorn, SQLAlchemy and aiogram are routed
6  + through the same structlog pipeline so the output stays homogeneous.
7  + """
8  +
9  + from __future__ import annotations
10 +
11 + import logging
12 + import sys
13 + from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Final
14 +
15 + import structlog
16 +
17 + from app.core.config import LogFormat
18 +
19 + if TYPE_CHECKING:
20 +     from structlog.typing import Processor
21 +
22 + _THIRD_PARTY_LOGGERS: Final = (
23 +     "uvicorn",
24 +     "uvicorn.error",
25 +     "uvicorn.access",
26 +     "fastapi",
27 +     "sqlalchemy.engine",
28 +     "sqlalchemy.pool",
29 +     "alembic",
30 +     "aiogram",
31 +     "aiogram.event",
32 +     "httpx",
33 + )
34 +
35 +
36 + def _shared_processors() -> list[Processor]:
37 +     return [
38 +         structlog.contextvars.merge_contextvars,
39 +         structlog.stdlib.add_log_level,
40 +         structlog.stdlib.add_logger_name,
41 +         structlog.processors.TimeStamper(fmt="iso", utc=True),
42 +         structlog.processors.StackInfoRenderer(),
43 +         structlog.processors.UnicodeDecoder(),
44 +     ]
45 +
46 +
47 + def _renderer(log_format: LogFormat) -> Processor:
48 +     if log_format is LogFormat.JSON:
49 +         return structlog.processors.JSONRenderer()
50 +     return structlog.dev.ConsoleRenderer(colors=True)
51 +
52 +
53 + def configure_logging(*, level: str, log_format: LogFormat) -> None:
54 +     """Configure structlog and the standard library root logger.
55 +
56 +     Idempotent: calling it twice (application factory plus bot entrypoint in the
57 +     same process) simply replaces the root handler.
58 +     """
59 +     numeric_level = logging.getLevelNamesMapping()[level.upper()]
60 +     shared = _shared_processors()
61 +
62 +     structlog.configure(
63 +         processors=[*shared, structlog.stdlib.ProcessorFormatter.wrap_for_formatter],
64 +         logger_factory=structlog.stdlib.LoggerFactory(),
65 +         wrapper_class=structlog.make_filtering_bound_logger(numeric_level),
66 +         cache_logger_on_first_use=True,
67 +     )
68 +
69 +     formatter = structlog.stdlib.ProcessorFormatter(
70 +         foreign_pre_chain=shared,
71 +         processors=[
72 +             structlog.stdlib.ProcessorFormatter.remove_processors_meta,
73 +             structlog.processors.format_exc_info,
74 +             _renderer(log_format),
75 +         ],
76 +     )
77 +
78 +     handler = logging.StreamHandler(sys.stdout)
79 +     handler.setFormatter(formatter)
80 +
81 +     root = logging.getLogger()
82 +     for existing in root.handlers[:]:
83 +         root.removeHandler(existing)
84 +     root.addHandler(handler)
85 +     root.setLevel(numeric_level)
86 +
87 +     for name in _THIRD_PARTY_LOGGERS:
88 +         third_party = logging.getLogger(name)
89 +         third_party.handlers = []
90 +         third_party.propagate = True
91 +
92 +     # SQL statement logging is controlled by POSTGRES_ECHO, never by log level.
93 +     logging.getLogger("sqlalchemy.engine").setLevel(logging.WARNING)
94 +
95 +
96 + def get_logger(name: str) -> structlog.stdlib.BoundLogger:
97 +     """Return a bound structlog logger for the given module name."""
98 +     return structlog.stdlib.get_logger(name)

    - """Bonus arithmetic and the checkout pricing port.
    -
    - Two things live here, and both are deliberately free of infrastructure:
    -
    - * the **money maths** — pure functions, so the rules that decide what a buyer is
    -   charged can be read, reviewed and tested without a database;
    - * the **ports** through which the purchase and delivery services reach the
    -   referral feature, so those services keep working unchanged when the ports are
    -   not wired in.
    -
    - **One bonus is one Telegram Star.** That is not a configured rate, it is the
    - model: the balance is a count of Stars' worth of discount, and it is spendable
    - only on a Stars purchase. ``PriceQuote.bonus_amount`` is therefore *derived*
    - from the unit count rather than stored beside it, so the two can never disagree.
    -
    - A purchase settled in USDT still earns its inviter a reward, and the Stars
    - equivalent comes from the **product's own two prices** at the moment of the sale
    - (``Product.stars_per_usdt``). The shop has already declared that equivalence by
    - pricing the item in both currencies, so no external price feed is involved, and
    - no fixed rate can silently go stale. The rate actually used is written onto the
    - ledger entry, which is what keeps an old reward from being recomputed after the
    - admin repriced the product.
    -
    - Rounding always favours the shop: a discount is floored and a reward is floored.
    - The reason is arithmetic safety rather than greed — ``price_stars`` is an
    - ``Integer`` column and the Stars gateway sends ``int(Decimal(amount))``, so if
    - rounding could go the other way a fraction of a Star would vanish silently
    - between the quote and the invoice.
    - """

    -

1   + """Bonus arithmetic and the checkout pricing port.
2   +
3   + Two things live here, and both are deliberately free of infrastructure:
4   +
5   + * the **money maths** — pure functions, so the rules that decide what a buyer is
6   +   charged can be read, reviewed and tested without a database;
7   + * the **ports** through which the purchase and delivery services reach the
8   +   referral feature, so those services keep working unchanged when the ports are
9   +   not wired in.
10  +
11  + **One bonus is one Telegram Star.** That is not a configured rate, it is the
12  + model: the balance is a count of Stars' worth of discount, and it is spendable
13  + only on a Stars purchase. ``PriceQuote.bonus_amount`` is therefore *derived*
14  + from the unit count rather than stored beside it, so the two can never disagree.
15  +
16  + A purchase settled in USDT still earns its inviter a reward, and the Stars
17  + equivalent comes from the **product's own two prices** at the moment of the sale
18  + (``Product.stars_per_usdt``). The shop has already declared that equivalence by
19  + pricing the item in both currencies, so no external price feed is involved, and
20  + no fixed rate can silently go stale. The rate actually used is written onto the
21  + ledger entry, which is what keeps an old reward from being recomputed after the
22  + admin repriced the product.
23  +
24  + Rounding always favours the shop: a discount is floored and a reward is floored.
25  + The reason is arithmetic safety rather than greed — ``price_stars`` is an
26  + ``Integer`` column and the Stars gateway sends ``int(Decimal(amount))``, so if
27  + rounding could go the other way a fraction of a Star would vanish silently
28  + between the quote and the invoice.
29  + """
30  +
31  + from __future__ import annotations
32  +
33  + from dataclasses import dataclass
34  + from decimal import ROUND_FLOOR, Decimal
35  + from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Final, Protocol
36  +
37  + from app.domain.enums import Currency
38  +
39  + if TYPE_CHECKING:
40  +     from uuid import UUID
41  +
42  +     from app.core.config import ReferralSettings
43  +     from app.domain.entities import Purchase
44  +     from app.domain.uow import UnitOfWork
45  +
46  + _PERCENT: Final = Decimal(100)
47  +
48  + _PRICE_STEP: Final[dict[Currency, Decimal]] = {
49  +     Currency.XTR: Decimal(1),
50  +     Currency.USDT: Decimal("0.01"),
51  + }
52  + """Smallest amount each currency can actually be charged in."""
53  +
54  +
55  + def price_step(currency: Currency) -> Decimal:
56  +     """Smallest chargeable amount in this currency."""
57  +     return _PRICE_STEP[currency]
58  +
59  +
60  + def floor_to_step(value: Decimal, currency: Currency) -> Decimal:
61  +     """Round down to something the provider can charge."""
62  +     step = price_step(currency)
63  +     return (value / step).to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_FLOOR) * step
64  +
65  +
66  + @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True, kw_only=True)
67  + class BonusPolicy:
68  +     """The configured percentages, lifted out of settings into the domain.
69  +
70  +     Taking a small value object rather than the whole settings tree keeps the
71  +     maths callable from a test with three literals. Note what is *absent*: no
72  +     exchange rate, because one bonus is one Star by definition.
73  +     """
74  +
75  +     discount_percent: int = 10
76  +     reward_percent: int = 15
77  +     max_bonus_payment_percent: int = 50
78  +
79  +     @classmethod
80  +     def from_settings(cls, settings: ReferralSettings) -> BonusPolicy:
81  +         """Build the policy from the process configuration."""
82  +         return cls(
83  +             discount_percent=settings.discount_percent,
84  +             reward_percent=settings.reward_percent,
85  +             max_bonus_payment_percent=settings.max_bonus_payment_percent,
86  +         )
87  +
88  +
89  + @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True, kw_only=True)
90  + class PriceQuote:
91  +     """What the buyer will actually be charged, and why.
92  +
93  +     Kept as an explicit breakdown rather than a single number because the
94  +     purchase row stores all three: what the product cost, what was taken off,
95  +     and what was billed. A later price change must not rewrite an old sale.
96  +     """
97  +
98  +     base_amount: Decimal
99  +     """The product's list price at the moment of checkout."""
100 +
101 +     discount_amount: Decimal = Decimal(0)
102 +     """Referral discount, in the purchase currency."""
103 +
104 +     bonus_units: int = 0
105 +     """Bonuses spent. Non-zero on a Stars purchase, or a USDT one with a rate."""
106 +
107 +     currency: Currency = Currency.XTR
108 +     referral_id: UUID | None = None
109 +     """The relationship the discount came from, if any."""
110 +
111 +     bonus_rate: Decimal | None = None
112 +     """Stars-per-USDT rate that values the bonus units on a USDT sale.
113 +
114 +     ``None`` on a Stars purchase, where one bonus is one Star and no rate is
115 +     needed. On a USDT purchase it is the product's own ``stars_per_usdt`` at the
116 +     moment of checkout, so the money value of the units is *derived* from the
117 +     same declared equivalence the reward already uses — never a fixed or
118 +     external rate that could go stale.
119 +     """
120 +
121 +     @property
122 +     def bonus_amount(self) -> Decimal:
123 +         """Money value of the bonuses spent, in the purchase currency.
124 +
125 +         Derived, not stored, so it can never disagree with the unit count. On
126 +         Stars one bonus is one Star. On USDT the units are converted at the
127 +         product's own rate and floored to a chargeable cent — rounding down, so
128 +         a fraction of a cent can never vanish between the quote and the invoice.
129 +         """
130 +         if self.bonus_units <= 0:
131 +             return Decimal(0)
132 +         if self.currency is Currency.XTR:
133 +             return Decimal(self.bonus_units)
134 +         if self.bonus_rate is None or self.bonus_rate <= 0:  # pragma: no cover — guarded upstream
135 +             return Decimal(0)
136 +         return floor_to_step(Decimal(self.bonus_units) / self.bonus_rate, self.currency)
137 +
138 +     @property
139 +     def charged_amount(self) -> Decimal:
140 +         """What the invoice is issued for."""
141 +         return self.base_amount - self.discount_amount - self.bonus_amount
142 +
143 +     @property
144 +     def uses_discount(self) -> bool:
145 +         """Whether a referral discount was applied."""
146 +         return self.discount_amount > 0
147 +
148 +     @property
149 +     def uses_bonus(self) -> bool:
150 +         """Whether any bonuses were spent."""
151 +         return self.bonus_units > 0
152 +
153 +     @property
154 +     def is_plain(self) -> bool:
155 +         """Whether this is an ordinary, unmodified sale."""
156 +         return not self.uses_discount and not self.uses_bonus
157 +
158 +
159 + def plain_quote(base_amount: Decimal, currency: Currency) -> PriceQuote:
160 +     """The quote of a shop without a referral programme: list price, no changes."""
161 +     return PriceQuote(base_amount=base_amount, currency=currency)
162 +
163 +
164 + def discount_for(base_amount: Decimal, currency: Currency, policy: BonusPolicy) -> Decimal:
165 +     """Referral discount on a first purchase, rounded down."""
166 +     if policy.discount_percent <= 0:
167 +         return Decimal(0)
168 +     raw = base_amount * Decimal(policy.discount_percent) / _PERCENT
169 +     return floor_to_step(raw, currency)
170 +
171 +
172 + def stars_equivalent(
173 +     paid_amount: Decimal,
174 +     currency: Currency,
175 +     *,
176 +     stars_per_usdt: Decimal | None,
177 + ) -> Decimal | None:
178 +     """What a settled payment is worth in Telegram Stars.
179 +
180 +     A Stars payment is already in Stars. A USDT payment needs the rate the
181 +     product itself declared; without one there is nothing to convert with, and
182 +     ``None`` says so rather than guessing.
183 +     """
184 +     if currency is Currency.XTR:
185 +         return paid_amount
186 +     if stars_per_usdt is None or stars_per_usdt <= 0:
187 +         return None
188 +     return paid_amount * stars_per_usdt
189 +
190 +
191 + def reward_bonuses(
192 +     paid_amount: Decimal,
193 +     currency: Currency,
194 +     *,
195 +     policy: BonusPolicy,
196 +     stars_per_usdt: Decimal | None = None,
197 + ) -> int:
198 +     """Bonuses earned by the inviter from one settled purchase.
199 +
200 +     The base is what the buyer *actually paid*, never the list price: a buyer
201 +     who paid 900 Stars after a discount earns the inviter 135, not 150.
202 +
203 +     Returns ``0`` when a USDT purchase carries no declared rate — the caller
204 +     logs that and credits nothing, which is safer than inventing a rate.
205 +     """
206 +     if policy.reward_percent <= 0:
207 +         return 0
208 +     stars = stars_equivalent(paid_amount, currency, stars_per_usdt=stars_per_usdt)
209 +     if stars is None or stars <= 0:
210 +         return 0
211 +     earned = stars * Decimal(policy.reward_percent) / _PERCENT
212 +     return int(earned.to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_FLOOR))
213 +
214 +
215 + def max_bonus_payment(base_amount: Decimal, policy: BonusPolicy) -> int:
216 +     """Largest number of bonuses allowed against this Stars price.
217 +
218 +     Read straight off the price because one bonus is one Star: 1000 ⭐ at 50%
219 +     accepts 500 bonuses, 600 ⭐ accepts 300, 200 ⭐ accepts 100.
220 +     """
221 +     if policy.max_bonus_payment_percent <= 0:
222 +         return 0
223 +     raw = base_amount * Decimal(policy.max_bonus_payment_percent) / _PERCENT
224 +     return int(raw.to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_FLOOR))
225 +
226 +
227 + def spendable_bonuses(
228 +     base_amount: Decimal,
229 +     currency: Currency,
230 +     *,
231 +     balance: int,
232 +     policy: BonusPolicy,
233 +     stars_per_usdt: Decimal | None = None,
234 + ) -> int:
235 +     """Bonuses the buyer may spend on this price.
236 +
237 +     Bounded by the same three things on every rail: the balance, the configured
238 +     share of the price, and the requirement that something is still left to
239 +     charge — the purchases table refuses a zero amount, and an invoice for
240 +     nothing is not a sale.
241 +
242 +     On Telegram Stars one bonus is one Star, so the cap is read straight off the
243 +     price. On USDT a bonus is still one Star, but the price is in dollars: the
244 +     units are valued at the product's own ``stars_per_usdt`` rate, so the cap is
245 +     the number of one-Star units whose floored dollar value stays within the
246 +     allowed share of the price. Without a rate — a product priced in USDT only —
247 +     there is no declared equivalence, and nothing can be spent.
248 +     """
249 +     if balance <= 0 or policy.max_bonus_payment_percent <= 0:
250 +         return 0
251 +
252 +     if currency is Currency.XTR:
253 +         payable = min(balance, max_bonus_payment(base_amount, policy))
254 +         # Leave at least one Star to actually charge.
255 +         payable = min(payable, int(base_amount) - 1)
256 +         return max(payable, 0)
257 +
258 +     if stars_per_usdt is None or stars_per_usdt <= 0:
259 +         return 0
260 +
261 +     # The most a bonus discount may be worth here, as a chargeable dollar
262 +     # amount — and never the whole price, so at least one cent is always billed.
263 +     max_discount = floor_to_step(
264 +         base_amount * Decimal(policy.max_bonus_payment_percent) / _PERCENT,
265 +         currency,
266 +     )
267 +     max_discount = min(max_discount, base_amount - price_step(currency))
268 +     if max_discount <= 0:
269 +         return 0
270 +
271 +     # …then the whole number of one-Star units that dollar amount buys.
272 +     max_units = int((max_discount * stars_per_usdt).to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_FLOOR))
273 +     return max(min(balance, max_units), 0)
274 +
275 +
276 + def quote(  # noqa: PLR0913 — pricing genuinely depends on this many inputs
277 +     base_amount: Decimal,
278 +     currency: Currency,
279 +     *,
280 +     policy: BonusPolicy,
281 +     referral_id: UUID | None = None,
282 +     discount_eligible: bool = False,
283 +     balance: int = 0,
284 +     use_bonus: bool = False,
285 +     stars_per_usdt: Decimal | None = None,
286 + ) -> PriceQuote:
287 +     """Price one checkout.
288 +
289 +     The referral discount and bonus spending are mutually exclusive by design:
290 +     the discount exists only on a buyer's first qualifying purchase, and on that
291 +     purchase bonuses are not offered at all. That keeps the economics simple and
292 +     removes a whole family of edge cases — after the first purchase the discount
293 +     is gone for good and bonuses apply from then on.
294 +
295 +     ``stars_per_usdt`` is the product's own rate, needed only to value bonuses on
296 +     a USDT sale; it is ignored on Stars and when no bonuses are spent.
297 +     """
298 +     if discount_eligible:
299 +         discount = discount_for(base_amount, currency, policy)
300 +         if discount > 0:
301 +             return PriceQuote(
302 +                 base_amount=base_amount,
303 +                 discount_amount=discount,
304 +                 currency=currency,
305 +                 referral_id=referral_id,
306 +             )
307 +
308 +     if use_bonus:
309 +         spent = spendable_bonuses(
310 +             base_amount,
311 +             currency,
312 +             balance=balance,
313 +             policy=policy,
314 +             stars_per_usdt=stars_per_usdt,
315 +         )
316 +         if spent > 0:
317 +             return PriceQuote(
318 +                 base_amount=base_amount,
319 +                 bonus_units=spent,
320 +                 currency=currency,
321 +                 bonus_rate=stars_per_usdt if currency is not Currency.XTR else None,
322 +             )
323 +
324 +     return plain_quote(base_amount, currency)
325 +
326 +
327 + class CheckoutPricing(Protocol):
328 +     """How the purchase service asks the referral feature what to charge.
329 +
330 +     ``resolve`` and ``hold_for`` take the caller's unit of work: pricing and the
331 +     reservation of bonuses must commit in the *same* transaction as the purchase
332 +     they belong to, otherwise a crash between the two could bill a buyer for an
333 +     amount whose funding was never recorded.
334 +     """
335 +
336 +     async def resolve(  # noqa: PLR0913 — one checkout, this many pricing facts
337 +         self,
338 +         uow: UnitOfWork,
339 +         *,
340 +         user_id: int,
341 +         base_amount: Decimal,
342 +         currency: Currency,
343 +         use_bonus: bool,
344 +         stars_per_usdt: Decimal | None = None,
345 +     ) -> PriceQuote:
346 +         """Price a checkout and hold whatever it needs to be funded.
347 +
348 +         ``stars_per_usdt`` is the product's own rate, passed so bonuses can be
349 +         valued on a USDT sale; it is ignored on Stars.
350 +
351 +         Raises:
352 +             InsufficientBonusBalanceError: the buyer asked to spend bonuses they
353 +                 no longer have — the balance moved between the prompt and the
354 +                 button press.
355 +             BonusesNotAvailableError: bonuses were requested on a rail that
356 +                 cannot spend them (a USDT product with no declared rate).
357 +         """
358 +         ...
359 +
360 +     async def preview(
361 +         self,
362 +         *,
363 +         user_id: int,
364 +         base_amount: Decimal,
365 +         currency: Currency,
366 +         use_bonus: bool,
367 +         stars_per_usdt: Decimal | None = None,
368 +     ) -> PriceQuote:
369 +         """Price a checkout without holding anything. Read only.
370 +
371 +         Only a prediction: whoever acts on it must have ``resolve`` re-derive
372 +         the number under a lock before a buyer is committed to it.
373 +         """
374 +         ...
375 +
376 +     @property
377 +     def discount_percent(self) -> int:
378 +         """Referral discount this shop gives, as a percentage."""
379 +         ...
380 +
381 +     async def discount_eligible(self, uow: UnitOfWork, user_id: int) -> bool:
382 +         """Whether this buyer's next purchase carries the referral discount.
383 +
384 +         Answered from the caller's transaction so the product card can show the
385 +         reduced price without a second round trip.
386 +         """
387 +         ...
388 +
389 +     async def hold_for(self, uow: UnitOfWork, purchase: Purchase, priced: PriceQuote) -> None:
390 +         """Record the hold behind a purchase that was just inserted.
391 +
392 +         Split from ``resolve`` only because the purchase id does not exist until
393 +         its row does; both run in the same transaction.
394 +         """
395 +         ...
396 +
397 +     async def on_payment_confirmed(self, uow: UnitOfWork, purchase: Purchase) -> None:
398 +         """Turn the holds behind a paid purchase into settled facts.
399 +
400 +         Releasing a hold has no hook here on purpose: invoices are expired in
401 +         bulk by housekeeping, so the release pass is a sweep rather than a
402 +         per-purchase callback.
403 +         """
404 +         ...
405 +
406 +
407 + class SaleCompletion(Protocol):
408 +     """How the delivery service reports a completed sale to the bonus feature.
409 +
410 +     Both methods are best effort by contract: the buyer already has their link
411 +     by the time either is called, so neither may fail a delivery.
412 +     """
413 +
414 +     async def accrue(self, purchase_id: UUID) -> None:
415 +         """Credit the buyer's inviter, if there is one. Idempotent."""
416 +         ...
417 +
418 +     async def invite_buyer(self, user_id: int) -> None:
419 +         """Offer the buyer the referral programme. Never required of them."""
420 +         ...
421 +

1   + """Domain entities.
2   +
3   + Immutable, infrastructure-free representations of the business objects. The
4   + persistence layer maps rows onto these; services and delivery layers never see
5   + SQLAlchemy models.
6   + """
7   +
8   + from __future__ import annotations
9   +
10  + from dataclasses import dataclass
11  + from decimal import Decimal
12  + from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Final
13  +
14  + from app.domain.enums import BonusTransactionType, Currency, PaymentProvider, PurchaseStatus
15  +
16  + if TYPE_CHECKING:
17  +     from datetime import datetime
18  +     from uuid import UUID
19  +
20  + _NO_MONEY: Final = Decimal(0)
21  + """Default for a money field that simply did not happen."""
22  +
23  +
24  + @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True, kw_only=True)
25  + class Product:
26  +     """A single digital good, reachable only through its deep link."""
27  +
28  +     id: UUID
29  +     slug: str
30  +     title: str
31  +     description: str
32  +     photo_file_id: str | None
33  +     delivery_url: str
34  +     price_stars: int | None
35  +     price_usdt: Decimal | None
36  +     is_active: bool
37  +     created_at: datetime
38  +     updated_at: datetime
39  +
40  +     def price_for(self, provider: PaymentProvider) -> int | Decimal | None:
41  +         """Price in the provider's own currency, or ``None`` when unsupported."""
42  +         if provider is PaymentProvider.STARS:
43  +             return self.price_stars
44  +         return self.price_usdt
45  +
46  +     def supports(self, provider: PaymentProvider) -> bool:
47  +         """Whether the product can be bought through this provider."""
48  +         return self.price_for(provider) is not None
49  +
50  +     @property
51  +     def available_providers(self) -> tuple[PaymentProvider, ...]:
52  +         """Providers with a configured price, in display order."""
53  +         return tuple(provider for provider in PaymentProvider if self.supports(provider))
54  +
55  +     @property
56  +     def stars_per_usdt(self) -> Decimal | None:
57  +         """How many Telegram Stars one USDT is worth *for this product*.
58  +
59  +         The shop declares this itself by pricing the item in both currencies, so
60  +         it needs no external price feed and no fixed rate that could go stale:
61  +         the two prices on the row already say what the merchant considers
62  +         equivalent. Used to express a USDT payment in Stars when crediting a
63  +         referral reward, and recorded on the ledger entry so repricing the
64  +         product later never recomputes an old reward.
65  +
66  +         ``None`` when the product carries only one of the two prices — there is
67  +         then no declared equivalence, and the caller credits nothing rather than
68  +         inventing a rate.
69  +         """
70  +         if self.price_stars is None or self.price_usdt is None or self.price_usdt <= 0:
71  +             return None
72  +         return Decimal(self.price_stars) / self.price_usdt
73  +

   - """Distributed lock contract.
   -
   - Locks are always bounded in time: a crashed process must never leave a buyer
   - permanently unable to purchase. The implementation stores the lock with an
   - expiry, and the holder releases it only if the stored token is still its own.
   - """
   -
   - from __future__ import annotations
   -
   - from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Final, Protocol
   -
   - if TYPE_CHECKING:
   -     from contextlib import AbstractAsyncContextManager
   -     from uuid import UUID
   -
   -     from app.domain.enums import PaymentProvider
   -
   - DEFAULT_LOCK_TTL_SECONDS: Final = 45.0
   - """Long enough for an invoice round trip, short enough to self-heal quickly."""
   -
   -
   - class LockManager(Protocol):
   -     """Acquires short lived, automatically expiring distributed locks."""
   -
   -     def lock(
   -         self,
   -         key: str,
   -         *,
   -         ttl_seconds: float | None = None,
   -         wait_seconds: float = 0.0,
   -     ) -> AbstractAsyncContextManager[None]:
   -         """Hold ``key`` for at most ``ttl_seconds``.
   -
   -         Args:

    - """Referral links and the rules that govern a referral relationship.
    -
    - A referral link is *not* a product link. It carries no product, opens no card
    - and sells nothing — it only records "B was invited by A". Afterwards B opens
    - ordinary product deep links, and the relationship keeps applying:
    -
    -     A invites B
    -       day 1 → /start ohhh
    -       day 3 → /start muse
    -       day 7 → /start xoxo
    -
    - Eligibility is therefore evaluated when a purchase is created, never when the
    - link is opened.
    - """

    -

    - from typing import Final

    -
    - REFERRAL_CODE_LENGTH: Final = 10
    - REFERRAL_CODE_MAX_LENGTH: Final = 16
    - """Stored column width. Longer than the generated code, so the code can grow."""
    -
    - _CODE_ALPHABET: Final = "abcdefghjkmnpqrstuvwxyz23456789"
    - """Lower-case base31 without ``i``, ``l``, ``o``, ``0`` and ``1``.
    -
    - A referral code is read off a screen and typed by humans, so the characters
    - that are routinely confused for one another are simply not in the alphabet.
    - 31 symbols over 10 positions is about 49 bits — not guessable by brute force
    - through a rate limited bot.
    - """
    -
    -

    -     """What happened when an invitation link was opened.

    -     opening your own is a user mistake, not a system failure.
    -     """
    -
    -     LINKED = "linked"
    -     """A new relationship was recorded and the discount is now available."""
    -
    -     ALREADY_LINKED = "already_linked"
    -     """This buyer already has a referrer; it is never overwritten."""
    -
    -     SELF_REFERRAL = "self_referral"
    -     """The inviter and the invited are the same Telegram account."""
    -
    -     NOT_ELIGIBLE = "not_eligible"
    -     """The buyer already has purchase history, so no relationship is created."""
    -
    -     UNKNOWN_CODE = "unknown_code"
    -     """The code belongs to nobody — a stale or mistyped link."""
    -
    -     DISABLED = "disabled"
    -     """The referral programme is switched off by configuration."""

1   + """Referral links and the rules that govern a referral relationship.
2   +
3   + A referral link is *not* a product link. It carries no product, opens no card
4   + and sells nothing — it only records "B was invited by A". Afterwards B opens
5   + ordinary product deep links, and the relationship keeps applying:
6   +
7   +     A invites B
8   +       day 1 → /start ohhh
9   +       day 3 → /start muse
10  +       day 7 → /start xoxo
11  +
12  + Eligibility is therefore evaluated when a purchase is created, never when the
13  + link is opened.
14  + """
15  +
16  + from __future__ import annotations
17  +
18  + import secrets
19  + from dataclasses import dataclass
20  + from enum import StrEnum
21  + from typing import Final
22  +
23  + REFERRAL_PAYLOAD_PREFIX: Final = "ref_"
24  + """Deep-link payload prefix that marks an invitation rather than a product."""
25  +
26  + REFERRAL_CODE_LENGTH: Final = 10
27  + REFERRAL_CODE_MAX_LENGTH: Final = 16
28  + """Stored column width. Longer than the generated code, so the code can grow."""
29  +
30  + _CODE_ALPHABET: Final = "abcdefghjkmnpqrstuvwxyz23456789"
31  + """Lower-case base31 without ``i``, ``l``, ``o``, ``0`` and ``1``.
32  +
33  + A referral code is read off a screen and typed by humans, so the characters
34  + that are routinely confused for one another are simply not in the alphabet.
35  + 31 symbols over 10 positions is about 49 bits — not guessable by brute force
36  + through a rate limited bot.
37  + """
38  +
39  +
40  + class ReferralOutcome(StrEnum):
41  +     """What happened when an invitation link was opened.
42  +
43  +     Every outcome is a normal, expected result: opening someone's link twice or
44  +     opening your own is a user mistake, not a system failure.
45  +     """
46  +
47  +     LINKED = "linked"
48  +     """A new relationship was recorded and the discount is now available."""
49  +
50  +     ALREADY_LINKED = "already_linked"
51  +     """This buyer already has a referrer; it is never overwritten."""
52  +
53  +     SELF_REFERRAL = "self_referral"
54  +     """The inviter and the invited are the same Telegram account."""
55  +
56  +     NOT_ELIGIBLE = "not_eligible"
57  +     """The buyer already has purchase history, so no relationship is created."""
58  +
59  +     UNKNOWN_CODE = "unknown_code"
60  +     """The code belongs to nobody — a stale or mistyped link."""
61  +
62  +     DISABLED = "disabled"
63  +     """The referral programme is switched off by configuration."""
64  +
65  +     @property
66  +     def is_linked(self) -> bool:
67  +         """Whether the buyer may now expect the first-purchase discount."""
68  +         return self is ReferralOutcome.LINKED
69  +
70  +
71  + @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True, kw_only=True)
72  + class ReferralRegistration:
73  +     """Result of opening an invitation link."""
74  +
75  +     outcome: ReferralOutcome
76  +     referrer_user_id: int | None = None
77  +
78  +     @property
79  +     def is_linked(self) -> bool:
80  +         """Whether a fresh relationship was created by this visit."""
81  +         return self.outcome.is_linked
82  +
83  +
84  + def generate_referral_code() -> str:
85  +     """Return a fresh, unpredictable referral code.
86  +
87  +     Built from ``secrets`` rather than the Telegram id: the code travels in a
88  +     public link, so it must not leak an account identifier, and it must not be
89  +     derivable from a username either.
90  +     """
91  +     return "".join(secrets.choice(_CODE_ALPHABET) for _ in range(REFERRAL_CODE_LENGTH))
92  +
93  +
94  + def referral_payload(code: str) -> str:
95  +     """Deep-link payload that records an invitation from this code's owner."""
96  +     return f"{REFERRAL_PAYLOAD_PREFIX}{code}"
97  +
98  +
99  + def is_referral_payload(payload: str) -> bool:
100 +     """Whether a ``/start`` payload looks like an invitation link."""
101 +     return payload.startswith(REFERRAL_PAYLOAD_PREFIX)
102 +
103 +
104 + def parse_referral_payload(payload: str) -> str | None:
105 +     """Extract the referral code from a payload, or ``None`` if it is not one.
106 +
107 +     Returning ``None`` for a malformed code (rather than raising) is what lets
108 +     the ``/start`` handler fall through to the ordinary product lookup: a
109 +     product whose slug happens to begin with ``ref_`` keeps working.
110 +     """
111 +     if not is_referral_payload(payload):
112 +         return None
113 +     code = payload[len(REFERRAL_PAYLOAD_PREFIX) :]
114 +     if not code or len(code) > REFERRAL_CODE_MAX_LENGTH:
115 +         return None
116 +     if not all(character in _CODE_ALPHABET for character in code):
117 +         return None
118 +     return code
119 +
120 +
121 + __all__ = [
122 +     "REFERRAL_CODE_LENGTH",
123 +     "REFERRAL_CODE_MAX_LENGTH",
124 +     "REFERRAL_PAYLOAD_PREFIX",
125 +     "ReferralOutcome",
126 +     "ReferralRegistration",
127 +     "generate_referral_code",
128 +     "is_referral_payload",
129 +     "parse_referral_payload",
130 +     "referral_payload",
131 + ]

1  + """Deep-link slug rules.
2  +
3  + The slug is the payload of ``https://t.me/<bot>?start=<slug>``, so it must obey
4  + Telegram's constraints: 1-64 characters from ``A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -``.
5  + """
6  +
7  + from __future__ import annotations
8  +
9  + import re
10 + from typing import Final
11 +
12 + from app.core.exceptions import InvalidSlugError
13 +
14 + SLUG_MAX_LENGTH: Final = 64
15 + SLUG_PATTERN: Final = r"^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$"
16 + _SLUG_RE: Final = re.compile(SLUG_PATTERN)
17 +
18 + RESERVED_SLUG_PREFIXES: Final = ("ref_",)
19 + """Deep-link prefixes that mean something other than "open this product"."""
20 +
21 +
22 + def is_valid_slug(value: str) -> bool:
23 +     """Return ``True`` when the value can be used as a deep-link payload."""
24 +     return bool(_SLUG_RE.match(value))
25 +
26 +
27 + def is_reserved_slug(value: str) -> bool:
28 +     """Whether this slug would collide with a non-product deep link.
29 +
30 +     ``ref_…`` payloads carry an invitation, not a product, so a product must not
31 +     be able to occupy that namespace. Only *new* slugs are checked: the
32 +     ``/start`` handler resolves an unknown ``ref_`` code by falling through to
33 +     the ordinary product lookup, so a slug that predates this rule keeps working.
34 +     """
35 +     return value.lower().startswith(RESERVED_SLUG_PREFIXES)
36 +
37 +
38 + def normalise_slug(value: str) -> str:
39 +     """Strip surrounding whitespace and validate the slug.
40 +
41 +     Raises:
42 +         InvalidSlugError: the value cannot be used in a Telegram deep link, or
43 +             it is reserved for a non-product payload.
44 +     """
45 +     candidate = value.strip()
46 +     if not is_valid_slug(candidate):
47 +         message = (
48 +             f"Slug must match {SLUG_PATTERN}: 1-{SLUG_MAX_LENGTH} characters "
49 +             f"from A-Z, a-z, 0-9, underscore and hyphen"
50 +         )
51 +         raise InvalidSlugError(message, slug=value)
52 +     if is_reserved_slug(candidate):
53 +         reserved = ", ".join(RESERVED_SLUG_PREFIXES)
54 +         message = f"Slug must not start with a reserved prefix ({reserved})"
55 +         raise InvalidSlugError(message, slug=value)
56 +     return candidate

21 +     """Reporting windows offered by the admin dashboard.

23 +     Windows are day aligned in UTC: ``TODAY`` starts at midnight today,

32 +     def start(self, now: datetime | None = None) -> datetime | None:
33 +         """Inclusive lower bound of the window, or ``None`` for all time."""
34 +         moment = (now or datetime.now(UTC)).astimezone(UTC)
35 +         midnight = moment.replace(hour=0, minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0)
36 +         match self:
37 +             case StatsPeriod.TODAY:
38 +                 return midnight
39 +             case StatsPeriod.WEEK:
40 +                 return midnight - timedelta(days=WEEK_DAYS - 1)
41 +             case StatsPeriod.MONTH:
42 +                 return midnight - timedelta(days=MONTH_DAYS - 1)
43 +             case StatsPeriod.ALL:
44 +                 return None

   -

1   + """Redis backed distributed locks with a mandatory expiry.
2   +
3   + Every lock is written with ``SET key token NX PX ttl``:
4   +
5   + * ``NX`` makes acquisition atomic — exactly one holder wins a race.
6   + * ``PX`` guarantees the lock disappears on its own. A process that crashes
7   +   between acquiring and releasing cannot block a buyer forever.
8   +
9   + Release is a compare-and-delete executed server side, so a holder whose TTL
10  + already expired can never delete a lock that now belongs to somebody else.
11  + """
12  +
13  + from __future__ import annotations
14  +
15  + import asyncio
16  + from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
17  + from time import monotonic
18  + from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Final
19  + from uuid import uuid4
20  +
21  + from app.core.exceptions import LockBusyError
22  + from app.core.logging import get_logger
23  +
24  + if TYPE_CHECKING:
25  +     from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
26  +
27  +     from redis.asyncio import Redis
28  +
29  +     from app.core.config import RedisSettings
30  +
31  + logger = get_logger(__name__)
32  +
33  + LOCK_KEY_PREFIX: Final = "lock:"
34  + _RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS: Final = 0.05
35  +
36  + # Delete the key only when it still holds our token.
37  + _RELEASE_SCRIPT: Final = """
38  + if redis.call('get', KEYS[1]) == ARGV[1] then
39  +     return redis.call('del', KEYS[1])
40  + end
41  + return 0
42  + """
43  +
44  +
45  + class RedisLockManager:
46  +     """Hands out short lived locks backed by Redis."""
47  +
48  +     def __init__(self, client: Redis, settings: RedisSettings) -> None:
49  +         self._client = client
50  +         self._default_ttl = settings.lock_ttl_seconds
51  +         self._default_wait = settings.lock_wait_seconds
52  +         self._release = client.register_script(_RELEASE_SCRIPT)
53  +
54  +     @asynccontextmanager
55  +     async def lock(
56  +         self,
57  +         key: str,
58  +         *,
59  +         ttl_seconds: float | None = None,
60  +         wait_seconds: float | None = None,
61  +     ) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
62  +         """Hold ``key`` for at most ``ttl_seconds``, then release it.
63  +
64  +         Raises:
65  +             LockBusyError: the lock stayed busy for the whole waiting window.
66  +         """
67  +         ttl = ttl_seconds if ttl_seconds is not None else self._default_ttl
68  +         wait = wait_seconds if wait_seconds is not None else self._default_wait
69  +         name = f"{LOCK_KEY_PREFIX}{key}"
70  +         token = uuid4().hex
71  +
72  +         if not await self._acquire(name, token, ttl=ttl, wait=wait):
73  +             logger.warning("lock_busy", lock_key=key, waited_seconds=wait)
74  +             raise LockBusyError(lock_key=key)
75  +
76  +         try:
77  +             yield
78  +         finally:
79  +             await self._release_safely(name, token, key)
80  +
81  +     async def _acquire(self, name: str, token: str, *, ttl: float, wait: float) -> bool:
82  +         deadline = monotonic() + wait
83  +         while True:
84  +             # At least one millisecond: px=0 would be rejected by Redis.
85  +             acquired = await self._client.set(name, token, nx=True, px=max(1, int(ttl * 1000)))
86  +             if acquired:
87  +                 return True
88  +             if monotonic() >= deadline:
89  +                 return False
90  +             await asyncio.sleep(_RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS)
91  +
92  +     async def _release_safely(self, name: str, token: str, key: str) -> None:
93  +         released = await self._release(keys=[name], args=[token])
94  +         if not released:
95  +             # The TTL fired before we finished: the work took longer than the
96  +             # lock's lifetime. Worth knowing about — it means the TTL is too low.
97  +             logger.warning("lock_expired_before_release", lock_key=key)
98  +
99  +     async def ttl(self, key: str) -> int:
100 +         """Remaining lifetime of a lock in milliseconds (diagnostics only)."""
101 +         return int(await self._client.pttl(f"{LOCK_KEY_PREFIX}{key}"))

8  +

19 +
20 +
21 + class RedisRateLimiter:
22 +     """Counts attempts per key inside a fixed time window."""
23 +
24 +     def __init__(self, client: Redis) -> None:
25 +         self._client = client
26 +
27 +     async def hit(self, key: str, *, limit: int, window_seconds: float) -> bool:
28 +         """Register an attempt; return ``True`` while the caller is under the limit."""
29 +         name = f"{RATE_LIMIT_KEY_PREFIX}{key}"
30 +         pipeline = self._client.pipeline()
31 +         pipeline.incr(name)
32 +         pipeline.pttl(name)
33 +         attempts, ttl = await pipeline.execute()
34 +
35 +         if int(ttl) < 0:
36 +             # First hit in this window (or a key without an expiry): set one.
37 +             await self._client.pexpire(name, max(1, int(window_seconds * 1000)))
38 +
39 +         allowed = int(attempts) <= limit
40 +         if not allowed:
41 +             logger.warning("rate_limit_exceeded", rate_key=key, attempts=int(attempts))
42 +         return allowed
43 +
44 +     async def reset(self, key: str) -> None:
45 +         """Forget the attempts for a key (called after a successful login)."""
46 +         await self._client.delete(f"{RATE_LIMIT_KEY_PREFIX}{key}")

64 +         try:

66 +                 await connection.execute(text("SELECT 1"))
67 +         except (SQLAlchemyError, OSError) as error:
68 +             logger.warning("database_ping_failed", error=str(error))
69 +             return False
70 +         return True

1  + """Translation of database integrity errors into domain errors.
2  +
3  + A unique violation is a business outcome ("this slug is taken", "this buyer
4  + already owns the product"), not an infrastructure crash — so it is translated at
5  + the boundary instead of leaking SQLAlchemy exceptions upwards.
6  + """
7  +
8  + from __future__ import annotations
9  +
10 + from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
11 +
12 + if TYPE_CHECKING:
13 +     from sqlalchemy.exc import IntegrityError
14 +
15 +
16 + def violated_constraint(error: IntegrityError) -> str | None:
17 +     """Return the name of the constraint that rejected the statement."""
18 +     candidates = (error.orig, getattr(error.orig, "__cause__", None))
19 +     for candidate in candidates:
20 +         name = getattr(candidate, "constraint_name", None)
21 +         if isinstance(name, str) and name:
22 +             return name
23 +     return None
24 +
25 +
26 + def like_pattern(term: str) -> str:
27 +     """Escape LIKE wildcards so user input cannot alter the search semantics."""
28 +     escaped = term.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("%", "\\%").replace("_", "\\_")
29 +     return f"%{escaped}%"
30 +

32 + LIKE_ESCAPE = "\\"

1   + """SQLAlchemy models.
2   +
3   + Database-level invariants are enforced here rather than only in Python: money
4   + moves through this schema, so "one paid copy per user" and "an invoice id is
5   + recorded once" are constraints, not conventions.
6   + """
7   +
8   + from __future__ import annotations
9   +
10  + import enum
11  + from datetime import datetime
12  + from decimal import Decimal
13  + from typing import Final
14  + from uuid import UUID, uuid4
15  +
16  + from sqlalchemy import (
17  +     BigInteger,
18  +     Boolean,
19  +     CheckConstraint,
20  +     Enum,
21  +     ForeignKey,
22  +     Index,
23  +     Integer,
24  +     Numeric,
25  +     String,
26  +     Text,
27  +     UniqueConstraint,
28  +     text,
29  + )
30  + from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column, relationship
31  +
32  + from app.domain.enums import (
33  +     BonusTransactionType,
34  +     Currency,
35  +     PaymentProvider,
36  +     PurchaseStatus,
37  + )
38  + from app.domain.referrals import REFERRAL_CODE_MAX_LENGTH
39  + from app.domain.slug import SLUG_MAX_LENGTH, SLUG_PATTERN
40  + from app.infrastructure.db.base import Base, TimestampMixin
41  +
42  + USDT_PRECISION: Final = 12
43  + USDT_SCALE: Final = 2
44  +
45  + STARS_RATE_PRECISION: Final = 18
46  + STARS_RATE_SCALE: Final = 6
47  + """Width of the recorded Stars-per-USDT rate. Wide enough to never round it."""
48  +
49  + _ACCESS_STATUS_SQL: Final = "status IN ('paid', 'delivered')"
50  +
51  + #: Operator class that makes ``ILIKE '%term%'`` index-assisted.
52  + _TRGM_OPS: Final = "gin_trgm_ops"
53  +
54  +
55  + def _trigram_index(name: str, column: str) -> Index:
56  +     """A GIN trigram index for the admin panel's substring search.
57  +
58  +     A B-tree cannot serve ``ILIKE '%term%'`` — the pattern has no anchored
59  +     prefix — so without this the admin search degrades into a full table scan as
60  +     soon as the shop has real traffic.
61  +     """
62  +     return Index(name, column, postgresql_using="gin", postgresql_ops={column: _TRGM_OPS})
63  +
64  +
65  + def _enum_column[EnumT: enum.Enum](enum_class: type[EnumT], name: str) -> Enum:
66  +     """Native PostgreSQL enum storing the enum *values* (not member names)."""
67  +     return Enum(
68  +         enum_class,
69  +         name=name,
70  +         native_enum=True,
71  +         create_constraint=False,
72  +         validate_strings=True,
73  +         values_callable=lambda enum: [member.value for member in enum],
74  +     )
75  +
76  +
77  + class ProductModel(TimestampMixin, Base):
78  +     """A digital good reachable through exactly one deep link."""
79  +
80  +     __tablename__ = "products"
81  +
82  +     id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(primary_key=True, default=uuid4)
83  +     slug: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(SLUG_MAX_LENGTH), nullable=False)
84  +     title: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(255), nullable=False)
85  +     description: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(Text, nullable=False, server_default=text("''"))
86  +     photo_file_id: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(255), nullable=True)
87  +     delivery_url: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(Text, nullable=False)
88  +     price_stars: Mapped[int | None] = mapped_column(Integer, nullable=True)
89  +     price_usdt: Mapped[Decimal | None] = mapped_column(
90  +         Numeric(USDT_PRECISION, USDT_SCALE),
91  +         nullable=True,
92  +     )
93  +     is_active: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(
94  +         Boolean,
95  +         nullable=False,
96  +         server_default=text("true"),
97  +     )
98  +
99  +     purchases: Mapped[list[PurchaseModel]] = relationship(
100 +         back_populates="product",
101 +         passive_deletes=True,
102 +     )
103 +
104 +     __table_args__ = (
105 +         UniqueConstraint("slug", name="uq_products_slug"),
106 +         CheckConstraint(f"slug ~ '{SLUG_PATTERN}'", name="slug_format"),
107 +         CheckConstraint(
108 +             "price_stars IS NOT NULL OR price_usdt IS NOT NULL",
109 +             name="price_present",
110 +         ),
111 +         CheckConstraint("price_stars IS NULL OR price_stars > 0", name="price_stars_positive"),
112 +         CheckConstraint("price_usdt IS NULL OR price_usdt > 0", name="price_usdt_positive"),
113 +         Index("ix_products_is_active_created_at", "is_active", "created_at"),
114 +         _trigram_index("ix_products_title_trgm", "title"),
115 +         _trigram_index("ix_products_slug_trgm", "slug"),
116 +         _trigram_index("ix_products_description_trgm", "description"),
117 +     )

169 +         ForeignKey("users.telegram_id", ondelete="RESTRICT"),
170 +         nullable=False,
171 +     )
172 +     product_id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
173 +         ForeignKey("products.id", ondelete="RESTRICT"),
174 +         nullable=False,
175 +     )
176 +     provider: Mapped[PaymentProvider] = mapped_column(
177 +         _enum_column(PaymentProvider, "payment_provider"),
178 +         nullable=False,
179 +     )
180 +     status: Mapped[PurchaseStatus] = mapped_column(
181 +         _enum_column(PurchaseStatus, "purchase_status"),
182 +         nullable=False,
183 +         server_default=text("'pending'"),
184 +     )
185 +     amount: Mapped[Decimal] = mapped_column(nullable=False)
186 +     """What the buyer is billed. Unchanged by the referral feature."""
187 +
188 +     # How ``amount`` was reached. Nullable ``base_amount`` is what keeps the
189 +     # migration additive: rows written before this feature have no breakdown,
190 +     # and for those the billed amount *was* the list price.
191 +     base_amount: Mapped[Decimal | None] = mapped_column(nullable=True)
192 +     discount_amount: Mapped[Decimal] = mapped_column(
193 +         nullable=False,
194 +         server_default=text("0"),
195 +     )
196 +     bonus_amount: Mapped[Decimal] = mapped_column(
197 +         nullable=False,
198 +         server_default=text("0"),
199 +     )
200 +     currency: Mapped[Currency] = mapped_column(
201 +         _enum_column(Currency, "currency"),
202 +         nullable=False,
203 +     )
204 +     external_id: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(128), nullable=False)
205 +     telegram_charge_id: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(128), nullable=True)
206 +     delivered_url: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(Text, nullable=True)
207 +     created_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(server_default=text("now()"), nullable=False)
208 +     paid_at: Mapped[datetime | None] = mapped_column(nullable=True)
209 +     delivered_at: Mapped[datetime | None] = mapped_column(nullable=True)
210 +
211 +     user: Mapped[UserModel] = relationship(back_populates="purchases", lazy="raise")
212 +     product: Mapped[ProductModel] = relationship(back_populates="purchases", lazy="raise")
213 +
214 +     __table_args__ = (
215 +         # One provider invoice maps to exactly one purchase: replayed webhooks
216 +         # and duplicated Telegram updates cannot create a second row.
217 +         UniqueConstraint("provider", "external_id", name="uq_purchases_provider_external_id"),
218 +         # A user can hold at most one paid copy of a product. Enforced by the

2   +
3   + Two invariants are carried by the database rather than by application code,
4   + because both of them are the kind that a race would otherwise break:
5   +

7   +   A payment notification replayed five times credits one reward, not five: the

145 +         await self._session.flush()
146 +         await self._session.refresh(model)
147 +         return to_bonus_transaction(model)
148 +
149 +     async def release_hold(self, purchase_id: UUID) -> BonusTransaction | None:
150 +         """Give back a reservation for an invoice that was never paid.
151 +
152 +         Not a refund: nothing was ever charged. Idempotent through the unique
153 +         constraint on ``(purchase_id, type)``.
154 +         """
155 +         model = await self._hold(purchase_id)
156 +         if model is None or model.type is BonusTransactionType.BONUS_SPENT:
157 +             # Nothing reserved, or the units were genuinely spent on a paid
158 +             # purchase. A paid purchase's bonuses are never given back.
159 +             return None
160 +
161 +         return await self.add(
162 +             BonusTransactionDraft(
163 +                 user_id=model.user_id,
164 +                 amount=abs(model.amount),
165 +                 type=BonusTransactionType.BONUS_RESERVE_RELEASED,
166 +                 purchase_id=purchase_id,
167 +                 referral_id=model.referral_id,
168 +                 stars_per_usdt=model.stars_per_usdt,
169 +             )
170 +         )
171 +
172 +     async def recompute_balance(self, user_id: int) -> int:
173 +         """Sum the ledger from scratch, ignoring the cache."""
174 +         statement = select(func.coalesce(func.sum(BonusTransactionModel.amount), 0)).where(
175 +             BonusTransactionModel.user_id == user_id
176 +         )
177 +         return int((await self._session.scalar(statement)) or 0)
178 +
179 +     async def reward_total(self, user_id: int) -> int:
180 +         statement = select(func.coalesce(func.sum(BonusTransactionModel.amount), 0)).where(
181 +             BonusTransactionModel.user_id == user_id,
182 +             BonusTransactionModel.type == BonusTransactionType.REFERRAL_REWARD,
183 +         )
184 +         return int((await self._session.scalar(statement)) or 0)
185 +
186 +     async def purchases_awaiting_reward(self, *, limit: int = 100) -> tuple[UUID, ...]:
187 +         """Delivered purchases by invited buyers that carry no reward yet.
188 +
189 +         The safety net behind reward accrual. A process that died between
190 +         marking a sale delivered and crediting the inviter is repaired from
191 +         here, the same way a lost payment webhook is repaired by reconciliation.
192 +         """
193 +         recorded = select(BonusTransactionModel.purchase_id).where(
194 +             BonusTransactionModel.type == BonusTransactionType.REFERRAL_REWARD,
195 +             BonusTransactionModel.purchase_id.is_not(None),
196 +         )
197 +         statement = (
198 +             select(PurchaseModel.id)
199 +             .join(ReferralModel, ReferralModel.referred_user_id == PurchaseModel.user_id)
200 +             .where(
201 +                 PurchaseModel.status == PurchaseStatus.DELIVERED,
202 +                 PurchaseModel.id.not_in(recorded),
203 +             )
204 +             .order_by(PurchaseModel.delivered_at.asc())
205 +             .limit(limit)
206 +         )
207 +         return tuple((await self._session.execute(statement)).scalars().all())
208 +
209 +     async def stale_holds(self, *, limit: int = 100) -> tuple[UUID, ...]:
210 +         """Purchases holding reserved units that can no longer be paid for."""
211 +         statement = (
212 +             select(BonusTransactionModel.purchase_id)
213 +             .join(PurchaseModel, PurchaseModel.id == BonusTransactionModel.purchase_id)
214 +             .where(
215 +                 BonusTransactionModel.type == BonusTransactionType.BONUS_RESERVED,
216 +                 PurchaseModel.status.in_(_UNPAYABLE_STATUSES),
217 +             )
218 +             .order_by(BonusTransactionModel.created_at.asc())
219 +             .limit(limit)
220 +         )
221 +         rows = (await self._session.execute(statement)).scalars().all()
222 +         return tuple(row for row in rows if row is not None)
223 +
224 +     async def _hold(self, purchase_id: UUID) -> BonusTransactionModel | None:
225 +         """The reservation or spend recorded against this purchase, row locked."""
226 +         statement = (
227 +             select(BonusTransactionModel)
228 +             .where(
229 +                 BonusTransactionModel.purchase_id == purchase_id,
230 +                 BonusTransactionModel.type.in_(BONUS_HOLD_TYPES),
231 +             )
232 +             .with_for_update()
233 +         )
234 +         return (await self._session.execute(statement)).scalar_one_or_none()
235 +
236 +     async def _move_balance(self, user_id: int, amount: int) -> None:
237 +         """Apply a delta to the cached balance, in the database's own arithmetic.
238 +
239 +         Written as ``balance = balance + :delta`` rather than read-modify-write
240 +         so two concurrent credits cannot lose one another.
241 +         """
242 +         statement = (
243 +             update(UserModel)
244 +             .where(UserModel.telegram_id == user_id)
245 +             .values(bonus_balance=UserModel.bonus_balance + amount)
246 +             .returning(UserModel.telegram_id)
247 +         )
248 +         touched = (await self._session.execute(statement)).scalar_one_or_none()
249 +         if touched is None:
250 +             raise UserNotFoundError(telegram_id=user_id)
251 +
252 +
253 + __all__ = ["SqlAlchemyBonusRepository"]

38  +         statement = select(ProductModel).where(ProductModel.slug == slug)
39  +         if only_active:

45  +         conditions = self._conditions(filters)
46  +
47  +         total = await self._session.scalar(
48  +             select(func.count()).select_from(ProductModel).where(*conditions)
49  +         )
50  +         statement = (
51  +             select(ProductModel)
52  +             .where(*conditions)
53  +             .order_by(ProductModel.created_at.desc(), ProductModel.id.desc())
54  +             .limit(page.limit)
55  +             .offset(page.offset)
56  +         )
57  +         models = (await self._session.execute(statement)).scalars().all()
58  +         return Page(

60  +             total=total or 0,
61  +             limit=page.limit,

66  +         model = ProductModel(

68  +             title=draft.title,
69  +             description=draft.description,
70  +             delivery_url=draft.delivery_url,
71  +             photo_file_id=draft.photo_file_id,
72  +             price_stars=draft.price_stars,
73  +             price_usdt=draft.price_usdt,
74  +             is_active=draft.is_active,
75  +         )
76  +         # A SAVEPOINT keeps the surrounding transaction usable when the insert
77  +         # is rejected: the service layer, not the repository, owns the commit.
78  +         try:
79  +             async with self._session.begin_nested():

90  +         model = await self._session.get(ProductModel, product_id)
91  +         if model is None:
92  +             raise ProductNotFoundError(product_id=str(product_id))
93  +

95  +         if not applied:
96  +             return to_product(model)
97  +

112 +         if model is None:
113 +             raise ProductNotFoundError(product_id=str(product_id))
114 +

120 +         if purchases:
121 +             message = "Product has purchases and cannot be deleted; deactivate it instead"
122 +             raise ConflictError(message, product_id=str(product_id), purchases=purchases)
123 +
124 +         await self._session.delete(model)
125 +         await self._session.flush()

128 +         statement = select(func.count()).select_from(ProductModel)

131 +         return await self._session.scalar(statement) or 0

135 +         conditions: list[ColumnElement[bool]] = []
