1   + """The arithmetic that decides what a buyer is charged and what an inviter earns.
2   +
3   + These are the rules the shop's economics rest on, and they are pure functions,
4   + so they are tested here with literals rather than through a database. Every case
5   + below is a rule somebody could get wrong in a way that costs real money.
6   +
7   + The model in one line: **one bonus is one Telegram Star.**
8   + """
9   +
10  + from __future__ import annotations
11  +
12  + from decimal import Decimal
13  +
14  + import pytest
15  +
16  + from app.domain.bonuses import (
17  +     BonusPolicy,
18  +     discount_for,
19  +     max_bonus_payment,
20  +     plain_quote,
21  +     quote,
22  +     reward_bonuses,
23  +     spendable_bonuses,
24  +     stars_equivalent,
25  + )
26  + from app.domain.enums import Currency
27  +
28  + POLICY = BonusPolicy(
29  +     discount_percent=10,
30  +     reward_percent=15,
31  +     max_bonus_payment_percent=50,
32  + )
33  +
34  + STARS = Currency.XTR
35  + USDT = Currency.USDT
36  +
37  +
38  + # --- The referral discount
39  +
40  +
41  + def test_the_discount_is_ten_percent_of_the_list_price() -> None:
42  +     """The worked example from the specification: 1000 Stars becomes 900."""
43  +     assert discount_for(Decimal(1000), STARS, POLICY) == Decimal(100)
44  +
45  +
46  + def test_a_stars_discount_is_always_a_whole_number_of_stars() -> None:
47  +     """Telegram Stars are integers, so a fractional discount cannot exist.
48  +
49  +     Rounding down is what keeps ``int(Decimal(amount))`` in the Stars gateway
50  +     honest: 999 minus a floored 10% is 900, and no fraction disappears silently.
51  +     """
52  +     assert discount_for(Decimal(999), STARS, POLICY) == Decimal(99)
53  +     assert Decimal(999) - discount_for(Decimal(999), STARS, POLICY) == Decimal(900)
54  +
55  +
56  + def test_a_usdt_discount_is_rounded_down_to_a_cent() -> None:
57  +     """USDT is charged in hundredths; a third of a cent is not chargeable."""
58  +     assert discount_for(Decimal("12.35"), USDT, POLICY) == Decimal("1.23")
59  +
60  +
61  + def test_a_tiny_price_simply_gets_no_discount() -> None:
62  +     """One Star cannot be discounted by a tenth of a Star, so it is not."""
63  +     assert discount_for(Decimal(1), STARS, POLICY) == Decimal(0)
64  +
65  +
66  + def test_a_zero_percent_discount_is_no_discount() -> None:
67  +     """Configuring the programme off must not produce rounding artefacts."""
68  +     policy = BonusPolicy(discount_percent=0)
69  +     assert discount_for(Decimal(1000), STARS, policy) == Decimal(0)
70  +
71  +
72  + # --- The inviter's reward, from a Stars purchase
73  +
74  +
75  + def test_a_full_price_stars_purchase_earns_fifteen_percent() -> None:
76  +     """The specification's headline case: 1000 ⭐ paid earns 150 bonuses."""
77  +     assert reward_bonuses(Decimal(1000), STARS, policy=POLICY) == 150
78  +
79  +
80  + def test_the_reward_is_taken_from_what_was_actually_paid() -> None:
81  +     """A buyer who paid 900 after a discount earns the inviter 135, not 150.
82  +
83  +     Paying 15% of the list price would quietly overpay every inviter on every
84  +     discounted first purchase.
85  +     """
86  +     assert reward_bonuses(Decimal(900), STARS, policy=POLICY) == 135
87  +
88  +
89  + def test_every_later_purchase_earns_its_own_reward() -> None:
90  +     """The inviter earns from each settled purchase, not just the first."""
91  +     assert reward_bonuses(Decimal(1200), STARS, policy=POLICY) == 180
92  +     assert reward_bonuses(Decimal(700), STARS, policy=POLICY) == 105
93  +
94  +
95  + def test_a_stars_reward_is_floored() -> None:
96  +     """101 ⭐ at 15% is 15.15 bonuses, which is 15 bonuses."""
97  +     assert reward_bonuses(Decimal(101), STARS, policy=POLICY) == 15
98  +
99  +
100 + def test_a_reward_too_small_to_express_is_zero() -> None:
101 +     """Six Stars at 15% is 0.9 of a bonus, which is not a bonus."""
102 +     assert reward_bonuses(Decimal(6), STARS, policy=POLICY) == 0
103 +
104 +
105 + # --- The inviter's reward, from a USDT purchase
106 +
107 +
108 + def test_a_usdt_purchase_is_converted_through_the_products_own_rate() -> None:
109 +     """The specification's example: 10 USDT at 70 ⭐/USDT earns 105 bonuses.
110 +
111 +     The rate is not fetched from anywhere — it is what the shop itself declared
112 +     by pricing the product in both currencies.
113 +     """
114 +     assert stars_equivalent(Decimal(10), USDT, stars_per_usdt=Decimal(70)) == Decimal(700)
115 +     assert reward_bonuses(Decimal(10), USDT, policy=POLICY, stars_per_usdt=Decimal(70)) == 105
116 +
117 +
118 + def test_a_stars_purchase_needs_no_rate_at_all() -> None:
119 +     """It is already denominated in Stars."""
120 +     assert stars_equivalent(Decimal(900), STARS, stars_per_usdt=None) == Decimal(900)
121 +
122 +
123 + def test_a_usdt_reward_is_floored_to_a_whole_bonus() -> None:
124 +     """12.34 USDT at 70 ⭐/USDT is 863.8 ⭐; 15% of that is 129.57 → 129."""
125 +     earned = reward_bonuses(
126 +         Decimal("12.34"),
127 +         USDT,
128 +         policy=POLICY,
129 +         stars_per_usdt=Decimal(70),
130 +     )
131 +     assert earned == 129
132 +
133 +
134 + def test_a_usdt_purchase_without_a_declared_rate_earns_nothing() -> None:
135 +     """No rate means no conversion, and inventing one is not an option.
136 +
137 +     The service logs this and credits nothing; a product priced in USDT only
138 +     declares no equivalence for the shop to use.
139 +     """
140 +     assert stars_equivalent(Decimal(10), USDT, stars_per_usdt=None) is None
141 +     assert reward_bonuses(Decimal(10), USDT, policy=POLICY, stars_per_usdt=None) == 0
142 +
143 +
144 + @pytest.mark.parametrize("rate", [Decimal(0), Decimal(-1)])
145 + def test_a_nonsensical_rate_earns_nothing(rate: Decimal) -> None:
146 +     assert reward_bonuses(Decimal(10), USDT, policy=POLICY, stars_per_usdt=rate) == 0
147 +
148 +
149 + def test_a_zero_percent_reward_earns_nothing() -> None:
150 +     policy = BonusPolicy(reward_percent=0)
151 +     assert reward_bonuses(Decimal(1000), STARS, policy=policy) == 0
152 +
153 +
154 + # --- How much of a price bonuses may cover
155 +
156 +
157 + def test_bonuses_cover_at_most_half_the_price() -> None:
158 +     """The specification's caps, read straight off the price."""
159 +     assert max_bonus_payment(Decimal(1000), POLICY) == 500
160 +     assert max_bonus_payment(Decimal(600), POLICY) == 300
161 +     assert max_bonus_payment(Decimal(200), POLICY) == 100

167 +

171 +     assert spendable_bonuses(Decimal(1000), STARS, balance=135, policy=POLICY) == 135
172 +
173 +
174 + def test_an_empty_balance_spends_nothing() -> None:

176 +

180 +
181 +     A product priced in USDT only declares no such rate, so nothing is spendable.

183 +     assert spendable_bonuses(Decimal("10.00"), USDT, balance=5000, policy=POLICY) == 0

199 +     assert spent == 350

202 + def test_something_is_always_left_to_charge() -> None:

346 + def test_the_breakdown_always_explains_the_charge() -> None:
347 +     """base - discount - bonus must equal what is billed.

1   + """Redis lock tests against a real Redis server.
2   +
3   + The properties that matter in production are checked here: exclusivity, the
4   + mandatory TTL, self-healing after a crash, safe release and waiting.
5   + """
6   +
7   + from __future__ import annotations
8   +

11  +

13  +
14  + from app.core.config import RedisSettings

16  + from app.infrastructure.cache.locks import LOCK_KEY_PREFIX, RedisLockManager
17  +

19  +     from redis.asyncio import Redis
20  +
21  + TTL = 0.5
22  +
23  +
24  + @pytest.fixture
25  + def locks(redis_client: Redis) -> RedisLockManager:
26  +     settings = RedisSettings(lock_ttl_seconds=5.0, lock_wait_seconds=0.0)
27  +     return RedisLockManager(redis_client, settings)
28  +
29  +
30  + async def test_only_one_holder_at_a_time(locks: RedisLockManager) -> None:
31  +     async with locks.lock("resource"):
32  +         with pytest.raises(LockBusyError) as error:
33  +             async with locks.lock("resource"):
34  +                 pass  # unreachable: acquisition raises
35  +         assert error.value.details["lock_key"] == "resource"
36  +
37  +
38  + async def test_the_lock_is_released_after_the_block(locks: RedisLockManager) -> None:
39  +     async with locks.lock("resource"):
40  +         pass
41  +     async with locks.lock("resource"):
42  +         pass  # a second acquisition proves the first one was released
43  +
44  +
45  + async def test_the_lock_is_released_even_when_the_body_raises(locks: RedisLockManager) -> None:
46  +     boom = RuntimeError("the critical section blew up")
47  +     with pytest.raises(RuntimeError):
48  +         async with locks.lock("resource"):
49  +             raise boom
50  +     async with locks.lock("resource"):
51  +         pass
52  +
53  +
54  + async def test_the_lock_carries_a_ttl(locks: RedisLockManager) -> None:
55  +     async with locks.lock("resource", ttl_seconds=30):
56  +         remaining = await locks.ttl("resource")
57  +     assert 0 < remaining <= 30_000
58  +
59  +

61  +     locks: RedisLockManager,
62  +     redis_client: Redis,
63  + ) -> None:
64  +     """Simulates a crashed holder: the key must vanish without anyone releasing it."""
65  +     await redis_client.set(f"{LOCK_KEY_PREFIX}resource", "other-holder", px=int(TTL * 1000))
66  +
67  +     with pytest.raises(LockBusyError):
68  +         async with locks.lock("resource"):
69  +             pass  # unreachable: acquisition raises
70  +
71  +     await asyncio.sleep(TTL + 0.15)
72  +     async with locks.lock("resource"):
73  +         pass
74  +
75  +
76  + async def test_releasing_does_not_delete_a_lock_owned_by_somebody_else(
77  +     locks: RedisLockManager,
78  +     redis_client: Redis,
79  + ) -> None:
80  +     """A holder whose TTL already expired must not delete the next holder's lock."""
81  +     key = f"{LOCK_KEY_PREFIX}resource"
82  +     async with locks.lock("resource", ttl_seconds=5):
83  +         # Somebody else took over the key while we were working.
84  +         await redis_client.set(key, "new-holder")
85  +     assert await redis_client.get(key) == "new-holder"
86  +
87  +

89  +     order: list[str] = []
90  +
91  +     async def holder() -> None:
92  +         async with locks.lock("resource", ttl_seconds=5):
93  +             order.append("holder-acquired")
94  +             await asyncio.sleep(0.2)
95  +         order.append("holder-released")
96  +
97  +     async def waiter() -> None:
98  +         await asyncio.sleep(0.05)
99  +         async with locks.lock("resource", ttl_seconds=5, wait_seconds=2.0):
100 +             order.append("waiter-acquired")
101 +

103 +     assert order == ["holder-acquired", "holder-released", "waiter-acquired"]

110 +                 pass  # unreachable: acquisition raises

114 +     async with locks.lock("first"), locks.lock("second"):
115 +         pass

118 + async def test_concurrent_contenders_are_serialised(locks: RedisLockManager) -> None:
119 +     """Twenty coroutines, one critical section: no interleaving is allowed."""
120 +     inside = 0
121 +     peak = 0
122 +     winners = 0
123 +
124 +     async def contend() -> None:
125 +         nonlocal inside, peak, winners
126 +         try:
127 +             async with locks.lock("resource", ttl_seconds=5, wait_seconds=3.0):
128 +                 winners += 1
129 +                 inside += 1

132 +                 inside -= 1

134 +             pass

138 +     assert winners == 20

149 +     assert await store.is_revoked("token-1") is True
150 +

     -     purchase and commits; the other then gets the lock, re-checks, and sees
     -     the pending discount — so it creates a full-price purchase instead.

     -             provider=PaymentProvider.STARS,
     -             external_id=uuid4().hex,
     -         )
     -
     -     purchase_a, purchase_b = await asyncio.gather(

     -         checkout(second_product),
     -     )

     -     # Both checkouts succeed (different products).
     -     assert purchase_a is not None
     -     assert purchase_b is not None
     -
     -     # Exactly one carries the discount.

     -         [purchase_a.discount_amount, purchase_b.discount_amount], reverse=True,
     -     )
     -     assert discounts == [Decimal(100), Decimal(0)], (

1    + """The referral and bonus feature end to end, on real PostgreSQL and Redis.
2    +
3    + These are the scenarios that decide whether the feature can be trusted with
4    + money. The fakes prove the rules; this file proves the constraints — a replayed
5    + webhook really cannot insert a second reward, and a discount really is burned
6    + once, because the database says so.
7    +
8    + The shop's own flow is asserted here too, unchanged: a buyer with no inviter
9    + pays the list price and receives their link exactly as before.
10   + """

62   + class RecordingNotifier:
63   +     """Captures the courtesy messages instead of sending them."""
64   +
65   +     def __init__(self, *, fail: bool = False) -> None:
66   +         self.rewards: list[RewardNotice] = []
67   +         self.hints: list[int] = []
68   +         self._fail = fail
69   +
70   +     async def notify_reward(self, notice: RewardNotice) -> None:
71   +         if self._fail:
72   +             message = "the inviter has blocked the bot"
73   +             raise RuntimeError(message)
74   +         self.rewards.append(notice)
75   +
76   +     async def notify_purchase_complete(self, user_id: int) -> None:
77   +         self.hints.append(user_id)

81   + class Shop:
82   +     """Every service wired over the live database and live Redis."""

95   +     return TelegramSettings(
96   +         bot_token=SecretStr(VALID_BOT_TOKEN),
97   +         bot_username="MyShopBot",

103  + def _build_shop(
104  +     uow_factory: SqlAlchemyUnitOfWorkFactory,
105  +     locks: RedisLockManager,
106  +     *,
107  +     referral: ReferralSettings,
108  +     notifier: RecordingNotifier | None = None,
109  + ) -> Shop:
110  +     recording = notifier or RecordingNotifier()
111  +     bonuses = BonusService(
112  +         uow_factory=uow_factory,
113  +         locks=locks,
114  +         settings=referral,
115  +         notifier=recording,
116  +     )
117  +     purchases = PurchaseService(uow_factory=uow_factory, locks=locks, pricing=bonuses)
118  +     gateway = FakeDeliveryGateway()
119  +     return Shop(
120  +         products=ProductService(uow_factory=uow_factory, telegram=_telegram()),
121  +         purchases=purchases,
122  +         delivery=DeliveryService(
123  +             uow_factory=uow_factory,
124  +             purchases=purchases,
125  +             gateway=gateway,
126  +             locks=locks,
127  +             settings=DeliverySettings(max_attempts=2, initial_backoff_seconds=0.01),
128  +             sale_completion=bonuses,
129  +         ),
130  +         referrals=ReferralService(
131  +             uow_factory=uow_factory,
132  +             telegram=_telegram(),
133  +             settings=referral,
134  +         ),
135  +         bonuses=bonuses,
136  +         gateway=gateway,
137  +         notifier=recording,
138  +         uow_factory=uow_factory,
139  +     )

161  + async def _buyers(shop: Shop, *profiles: UserDraft) -> None:
162  +     """The bot records a visitor when a card or an invitation opens."""
163  +     for profile in profiles:
164  +         await shop.purchases.remember_user(profile)

167  + async def _product(shop: Shop, **overrides: object) -> Product:
168  +     values: dict[str, object] = {
169  +         "slug": f"vip{uuid4().hex[:6]}",
170  +         "title": "VIP access",
171  +         "description": "Lifetime access",
172  +         "delivery_url": DELIVERY_URL,
173  +         "price_stars": STARS_PRICE,
174  +     }
175  +     values.update(overrides)
176  +     return await shop.products.create(ProductDraft(**values))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
177  +
178  +
179  + async def _invite(shop: Shop, inviter: UserDraft, invited: UserDraft) -> None:
180  +     """Mint the inviter's code and open it as the invited user."""
181  +     summary = await shop.referrals.summary(inviter)
182  +     registration = await shop.referrals.register(
183  +         payload=f"ref_{summary.referral_code}",
184  +         profile=invited,
185  +     )
186  +     assert registration.is_linked
187  +
188  +
189  + async def _buy(
190  +     shop: Shop,
191  +     buyer: UserDraft,
192  +     product: Product,
193  +     *,
194  +     use_bonus: bool = False,
195  + ) -> Purchase:
196  +     """One complete sale: invoice, payment, delivery."""
197  +     purchase = await shop.purchases.start_purchase(
198  +         user_id=buyer.telegram_id,
199  +         product_id=product.id,
200  +         provider=PaymentProvider.STARS,
201  +         external_id=uuid4().hex,
202  +         use_bonus=use_bonus,
203  +     )
204  +     await shop.purchases.confirm_payment(
205  +         provider=PaymentProvider.STARS,
206  +         external_id=purchase.external_id,
207  +     )
208  +     result = await shop.delivery.deliver_purchase(purchase.id)
209  +     assert result.succeeded
210  +     return await shop.purchases.get(purchase.id)
211  +
212  +
213  + async def _balance(shop: Shop, telegram_id: int) -> int:
214  +     return await shop.bonuses.balance_of(telegram_id)
215  +
216  +
217  + async def _ledger_types(shop: Shop, purchase_id: UUID) -> list[str]:
218  +     async with shop.uow_factory() as uow:
219  +         entry = await uow.bonuses.find_for_purchase(purchase_id)
220  +         return [] if entry is None else [entry.type.value]

334  +
335  + async def test_an_abandoned_invoice_does_not_burn_the_discount(shop: Shop) -> None:
336  +     """The discount is consumed when the payment lands, not when it is offered.
337  +
338  +     While a discounted checkout is active (PENDING), it holds the one-time
339  +     discount and blocks any other checkout from claiming it. Once that invoice
340  +     is abandoned and expires (EXPIRED), the discount is released so the buyer
341  +     can use it on a fresh purchase.
342  +     """
343  +     await _buyers(shop, INVITER, INVITED)
344  +     await _invite(shop, INVITER, INVITED)
345  +     abandoned = await _product(shop)
346  +     second_product = await _product(shop)
347  +     real = await _product(shop)
348  +
349  +     # 1. Start a discounted checkout. It is pending and holds the discount.
350  +     first_purchase = await shop.purchases.start_purchase(
351  +         user_id=INVITED.telegram_id,
352  +         product_id=abandoned.id,
353  +         provider=PaymentProvider.STARS,
354  +         external_id=uuid4().hex,
355  +     )
356  +     assert first_purchase.discount_amount == Decimal(100)
357  +
358  +     # 2. While the first checkout is PENDING, another checkout cannot claim the discount.
359  +     blocked_purchase = await shop.purchases.start_purchase(
360  +         user_id=INVITED.telegram_id,
361  +         product_id=second_product.id,
362  +         provider=PaymentProvider.STARS,
363  +         external_id=uuid4().hex,
364  +     )
365  +     assert blocked_purchase.discount_amount == Decimal(0)
366  +
367  +     # 3. The first invoice is abandoned and expires.
368  +     await shop.purchases.expire_stale(now=_far_future())
369  +
370  +     # 4. After expiration, a new checkout receives the discount and completes.
371  +     purchase = await _buy(shop, INVITED, real)
372  +     assert purchase.discount_amount == Decimal(100)
373  +

482  +
483  + @pytest.mark.parametrize("replays", [2, 5])
484  + async def test_a_replayed_payment_notification_credits_one_reward(
485  +     shop: Shop,
486  +     replays: int,
487  + ) -> None:
488  +     """Five identical webhooks must leave +135, never +675.
489  +
490  +     Guaranteed by ``uq_bonus_transactions_purchase_type``: the second insert
491  +     cannot exist, whatever the application layer attempts.
492  +     """
493  +     await _buyers(shop, INVITER, INVITED)
494  +     await _invite(shop, INVITER, INVITED)
495  +     product = await _product(shop)
496  +
497  +     purchase = await shop.purchases.start_purchase(
498  +         user_id=INVITED.telegram_id,
499  +         product_id=product.id,
500  +         provider=PaymentProvider.STARS,
501  +         external_id=uuid4().hex,
502  +     )
503  +     for _ in range(replays):
504  +         await shop.purchases.confirm_payment(
505  +             provider=PaymentProvider.STARS,
506  +             external_id=purchase.external_id,
507  +         )
508  +         await shop.delivery.deliver_purchase(purchase.id)
509  +

538  + async def test_a_missed_reward_is_repaired_by_housekeeping(
539  +     live_uow_factory: SqlAlchemyUnitOfWorkFactory,
540  +     live_locks: RedisLockManager,
541  +     referral_settings: ReferralSettings,
542  + ) -> None:
543  +     """Simulates a process that died after delivery but before the ledger write.
544  +
545  +     The sale is completed by a shop with no bonus hook at all, then a properly
546  +     wired one repairs it — which is the crash window this pass exists for.
547  +     """
548  +     blind = _build_shop(
549  +         live_uow_factory,
550  +         live_locks,
551  +         referral=referral_settings,
552  +     )
553  +     await _buyers(blind, INVITER, INVITED)
554  +     await _invite(blind, INVITER, INVITED)
555  +     product = await _product(blind)
556  +
557  +     purchase = await blind.purchases.start_purchase(
558  +         user_id=INVITED.telegram_id,
559  +         product_id=product.id,
560  +         provider=PaymentProvider.STARS,
561  +         external_id=uuid4().hex,
562  +     )
563  +     await blind.purchases.confirm_payment(
564  +         provider=PaymentProvider.STARS,
565  +         external_id=purchase.external_id,
566  +     )
567  +     # Deliver through a service that reports nothing to the bonus feature.
568  +     crashed = DeliveryService(
569  +         uow_factory=live_uow_factory,
570  +         purchases=blind.purchases,
571  +         gateway=FakeDeliveryGateway(),
572  +         locks=live_locks,
573  +         settings=DeliverySettings(max_attempts=2, initial_backoff_seconds=0.01),
574  +     )
575  +     assert (await crashed.deliver_purchase(purchase.id)).succeeded
576  +     assert await _balance(blind, INVITER.telegram_id) == 0
577  +
578  +     assert await blind.bonuses.accrue_missing() == 1
579  +     assert await _balance(blind, INVITER.telegram_id) == 135

754  +
755  + async def test_the_same_balance_cannot_fund_two_checkouts(shop: Shop) -> None:
756  +     """135 units, two products, two simultaneous checkouts: one wins.
757  +
758  +     Three defences stand behind this — the Redis lock on the balance, the row
759  +     lock on the users row, and the non-negative check constraint. The assertion
760  +     is simply that the balance never went below zero and only one sale was
761  +     funded.
762  +     """
763  +     await _buyers(shop, INVITER, INVITED)
764  +     await _invite(shop, INVITER, INVITED)
765  +     await _buy(shop, INVITED, await _product(shop))
766  +     assert await _balance(shop, INVITER.telegram_id) == 135
767  +
768  +     first = await _product(shop, price_stars=1000)
769  +     second = await _product(shop, price_stars=1000)
770  +
771  +     async def checkout(product: Product) -> Purchase | None:
772  +         try:
773  +             return await shop.purchases.start_purchase(
774  +                 user_id=INVITER.telegram_id,
775  +                 product_id=product.id,
776  +                 provider=PaymentProvider.STARS,
777  +                 external_id=uuid4().hex,
778  +                 use_bonus=True,
779  +             )
780  +         except Exception:
781  +             return None
782  +
783  +     results = await asyncio.gather(checkout(first), checkout(second))
784  +
785  +     funded = [purchase for purchase in results if purchase and purchase.bonus_amount > 0]
786  +     assert len(funded) == 1
787  +     assert await _balance(shop, INVITER.telegram_id) >= 0
788  +     assert await _balance(shop, INVITER.telegram_id) == 0
789  +
790  +
791  + async def test_the_ledger_always_explains_the_balance(shop: Shop) -> None:
792  +     """The cached balance is a cache, and it is provably one.
793  +
794  +     Reward, reservation, release and spend all move both the ledger and the
795  +     cached column in the same transaction, so recomputing from history must
796  +     always agree with the column.
797  +     """
798  +     await _buyers(shop, INVITER, INVITED)
799  +     await _invite(shop, INVITER, INVITED)
800  +     # Earn, then exercise every kind of ledger entry in turn: a reservation
801  +     # that is released, and a reservation that becomes a spend.
802  +     await _buy(shop, INVITED, await _product(shop, price_stars=1000))
803  +     await _buy(shop, INVITED, await _product(shop, price_stars=1200))
804  +
805  +     await shop.purchases.start_purchase(
806  +         user_id=INVITER.telegram_id,
807  +         product_id=(await _product(shop)).id,
808  +         provider=PaymentProvider.STARS,
809  +         external_id=uuid4().hex,
810  +         use_bonus=True,
811  +     )
812  +     await shop.purchases.expire_stale(now=_far_future())
813  +     await shop.bonuses.release_stale_holds()
814  +
815  +     await _buy(shop, INVITER, await _product(shop, price_stars=1000), use_bonus=True)
816  +
817  +     async with shop.uow_factory() as uow:
818  +         cached = await uow.bonuses.balance(INVITER.telegram_id)
819  +         recomputed = await uow.bonuses.recompute_balance(INVITER.telegram_id)
820  +     assert cached == recomputed
821  +
822  +
823  + def _far_future() -> datetime:
824  +     """A moment by which every invoice in a test has certainly expired."""
825  +     return datetime.now(UTC) + timedelta(days=1)
826  +
827  +
828  + # --- Rewards from a USDT purchase
829  +
830  +
831  + async def _buy_with_crypto(
832  +     shop: Shop,
833  +     buyer: UserDraft,
834  +     product: Product,
835  + ) -> Purchase:
836  +     """One complete USDT sale: invoice, payment, delivery.
837  +
838  +     ``expected_amount`` is passed because production passes it: the CryptoBot
839  +     invoice is raised before the purchase row exists, so the price is quoted
840  +     first and the purchase refuses to be recorded at any other number. A helper
841  +     that omitted it would quietly skip that check — which is exactly how a
842  +     discounted crypto checkout once shipped broken.
843  +     """
844  +     expected = await shop.purchases.quote_amount(
845  +         user_id=buyer.telegram_id,
846  +         product=product,
847  +         provider=PaymentProvider.CRYPTO,
848  +     )
849  +     purchase = await shop.purchases.start_purchase(
850  +         user_id=buyer.telegram_id,
851  +         product_id=product.id,
852  +         provider=PaymentProvider.CRYPTO,
853  +         external_id=uuid4().hex,
854  +         expected_amount=expected,
855  +     )
856  +     await shop.purchases.confirm_payment(
857  +         provider=PaymentProvider.CRYPTO,
858  +         external_id=purchase.external_id,
859  +     )
860  +     result = await shop.delivery.deliver_purchase(purchase.id)
861  +     assert result.succeeded
862  +     return await shop.purchases.get(purchase.id)
863  +

867  +
868  +     Used by the tests that want a *full price* purchase, since an invited
869  +     buyer's very first one is always discounted.
870  +     """
871  +     await _buy(shop, buyer, await _product(shop, price_stars=10, price_usdt=None))

880  +     70 ⭐ per USDT. A 10 USDT payment is therefore worth 700 ⭐, and 15% of that

912  + async def test_repricing_the_product_does_not_recompute_an_old_reward(
913  +     shop: Shop,
914  + ) -> None:
915  +     """The rule that makes historical bonuses trustworthy.
916  +
917  +     A reward earned at 70 ⭐/USDT stays what it was even after the admin moves
918  +     the product to 80 ⭐/USDT — the old entry keeps its own rate, and only the
919  +     next sale uses the new one.
920  +     """
921  +     await _buyers(shop, INVITER, INVITED, THIRD)
922  +     await _invite(shop, INVITER, INVITED)
923  +     await _invite(shop, INVITER, THIRD)
924  +     await _burn_discount(shop, INVITED)
925  +     await _burn_discount(shop, THIRD)
926  +     product = await _product(shop, price_stars=700, price_usdt=Decimal("10.00"))
927  +     first = await _buy_with_crypto(shop, INVITED, product)
928  +
929  +     from app.domain.commands import ProductUpdate  # noqa: PLC0415
930  +
931  +     await shop.products.update(product.id, ProductUpdate(price_stars=800))
932  +     second = await _buy_with_crypto(shop, THIRD, product)
933  +
934  +     async with shop.uow_factory() as uow:
935  +         old = await uow.bonuses.find_for_purchase(
936  +             first.id,
937  +             BonusTransactionType.REFERRAL_REWARD,
938  +         )
939  +         new = await uow.bonuses.find_for_purchase(
940  +             second.id,
941  +             BonusTransactionType.REFERRAL_REWARD,
942  +         )
943  +     assert old is not None
944  +     assert new is not None
945  +     # The old reward and its rate are untouched…
946  +     assert old.amount == 105
947  +     assert old.stars_per_usdt == Decimal(70)
948  +     # …while the new sale used the new rate: 800/10 gives 80, times 10 is 800, 15% is 120.
949  +     assert new.amount == 120
950  +     assert new.stars_per_usdt == Decimal(80)

986  +
987  + # --- Spending bonuses on a USDT purchase
988  + #
989  + # A bonus is priced in Stars, but a product that also carries a Stars price has
990  + # declared its own Stars/USDT rate, so the balance can be spent against a USDT
991  + # invoice at that rate. Everything the Stars rail promises must hold here too,
992  + # on real PostgreSQL and Redis: reserve then settle, release on expiry,
993  + # idempotent replay, referral priority, and one balance per checkout. A USDT
994  + # product priced in dollars only has no rate, so bonuses are refused on it.
995  +
996  +
997  + async def _grant_bonuses(shop: Shop, user_id: int, units: int) -> None:
998  +     """Seed an exact balance by crediting a reward straight to the ledger.
999  +
1000 +     The spend tests need a known starting balance to assert clean USDT
1001 +     arithmetic; earning it through a sale would tie the number to the reward
1002 +     formula instead. ``add`` moves the cached balance in the same transaction,
1003 +     exactly as a real reward would, so the balance under test is a real one.
1004 +     """
1005 +     async with shop.uow_factory() as uow:
1006 +         await uow.bonuses.add(
1007 +             BonusTransactionDraft(
1008 +                 user_id=user_id,
1009 +                 amount=units,
1010 +                 type=BonusTransactionType.REFERRAL_REWARD,
1011 +             )
1012 +         )
1013 +
1014 +
1015 + async def _buy_with_crypto_bonus(
1016 +     shop: Shop,
1017 +     buyer: UserDraft,
1018 +     product: Product,
1019 + ) -> Purchase:
1020 +     """A complete USDT sale that spends bonuses, priced the way production does.
1021 +
1022 +     ``use_bonus`` is carried through both the quote and the checkout, and the
1023 +     quoted amount is handed back as ``expected_amount`` — so the CryptoBot
1024 +     invoice and the recorded purchase are pinned to the same number, which is
1025 +     the crypto rail's whole contract.
1026 +     """
1027 +     expected = await shop.purchases.quote_amount(
1028 +         user_id=buyer.telegram_id,
1029 +         product=product,
1030 +         provider=PaymentProvider.CRYPTO,
1031 +         use_bonus=True,
1032 +     )
1033 +     purchase = await shop.purchases.start_purchase(
1034 +         user_id=buyer.telegram_id,
1035 +         product_id=product.id,
1036 +         provider=PaymentProvider.CRYPTO,
1037 +         external_id=uuid4().hex,
1038 +         use_bonus=True,
1039 +         expected_amount=expected,
1040 +     )
1041 +     await shop.purchases.confirm_payment(
1042 +         provider=PaymentProvider.CRYPTO,
1043 +         external_id=purchase.external_id,
1044 +     )
1045 +     result = await shop.delivery.deliver_purchase(purchase.id)
1046 +     assert result.succeeded
1047 +     return await shop.purchases.get(purchase.id)
1048 +

1281 + async def test_the_same_balance_cannot_fund_two_usdt_checkouts(shop: Shop) -> None:
1282 +     """One balance, two simultaneous USDT checkouts: exactly one is funded.
1283 +
1284 +     350 ⭐ funds the whole half-price cap of a single 700 ⭐ / 10 USDT product,
1285 +     so it cannot fund two. The row lock on the users row and the non-negative
1286 +     check constraint stand behind the assertion that the balance never goes
1287 +     below zero and only one sale reserves anything.
1288 +     """
1289 +     await _buyers(shop, INVITER)
1290 +     await _grant_bonuses(shop, INVITER.telegram_id, 350)
1291 +     first = await _product(shop, price_stars=700, price_usdt=Decimal("10.00"))
1292 +     second = await _product(shop, price_stars=700, price_usdt=Decimal("10.00"))
1293 +
1294 +     async def checkout(product: Product) -> Purchase | None:
1295 +         try:
1296 +             return await shop.purchases.start_purchase(
1297 +                 user_id=INVITER.telegram_id,
1298 +                 product_id=product.id,
1299 +                 provider=PaymentProvider.CRYPTO,
1300 +                 external_id=uuid4().hex,
1301 +                 use_bonus=True,
1302 +             )
1303 +         except Exception:
1304 +             return None
1305 +
1306 +     results = await asyncio.gather(checkout(first), checkout(second))
1307 +
1308 +     funded = [purchase for purchase in results if purchase and purchase.bonus_amount > 0]
1309 +     assert len(funded) == 1
1310 +     assert await _balance(shop, INVITER.telegram_id) >= 0
1311 +     assert await _balance(shop, INVITER.telegram_id) == 0

1422 + async def test_bug2_settlement_after_discount_burned_does_not_crash(
1423 +     shop: Shop,
1424 + ) -> None:
1425 +     """Bug #2 safety net: on_payment_confirmed catches DiscountAlreadyUsedError.
1426 +
1427 +     Scenario (legacy data or theoretical race that slipped past Bug #1's guard):
1428 +     two purchases were both created with ``discount_amount > 0``.  The first
1429 +     was paid and its settlement burned the referral's discount.  Settling the
1430 +     second must NOT raise — the purchase is already paid, the money moved, and
1431 +     refusing delivery would be worse than honouring the leaked discount.
1432 +
1433 +     What we verify:
1434 +     - payment is confirmed (purchase.status moves to PAID);
1435 +     - delivery succeeds (the buyer gets their link);
1436 +     - the original ``discount_purchase_id`` on the referral is unchanged;
1437 +     - a warning is logged (structlog capture is outside this test's scope, but
1438 +       the code path runs without raising).
1439 +     """
1440 +     await _buyers(shop, INVITER, INVITED)
1441 +     await _invite(shop, INVITER, INVITED)
1442 +     product_a = await _product(shop, price_stars=1000)
1443 +
1444 +     # Normal discounted purchase — burns the one-time discount.
1445 +     purchase_a = await shop.purchases.start_purchase(
1446 +         user_id=INVITED.telegram_id,
1447 +         product_id=product_a.id,
1448 +         provider=PaymentProvider.STARS,
1449 +         external_id=uuid4().hex,
1450 +     )
1451 +     assert purchase_a.discount_amount == Decimal(100)
1452 +     await shop.purchases.confirm_payment(
1453 +         provider=PaymentProvider.STARS,
1454 +         external_id=purchase_a.external_id,
1455 +     )
1456 +     result_a = await shop.delivery.deliver_purchase(purchase_a.id)
1457 +     assert result_a.succeeded
1458 +
1459 +     # Verify the discount is now burned, pointing at purchase A.
1460 +     async with shop.uow_factory() as uow:
1461 +         referral = await uow.referrals.get_by_referred(INVITED.telegram_id)
1462 +     assert referral is not None
1463 +     assert referral.discount_purchase_id == purchase_a.id
1464 +     assert not referral.discount_available
1465 +
1466 +     # Second purchase — with Bug #1 guard active, it gets full price.
1467 +     product_b = await _product(shop, price_stars=1000)
1468 +     purchase_b = await shop.purchases.start_purchase(
1469 +         user_id=INVITED.telegram_id,
1470 +         product_id=product_b.id,
1471 +         provider=PaymentProvider.STARS,
1472 +         external_id=uuid4().hex,
1473 +     )
1474 +     assert purchase_b.discount_amount == Decimal(0)
1475 +     assert purchase_b.amount == Decimal(1000)
1476 +
1477 +     # Confirm and deliver — must not raise.
1478 +     confirmed_b = await shop.purchases.confirm_payment(
1479 +         provider=PaymentProvider.STARS,
1480 +         external_id=purchase_b.external_id,
1481 +     )
1482 +     result_b = await shop.delivery.deliver_purchase(confirmed_b.id)
1483 +     assert result_b.succeeded
1484 +
1485 +     # The original discount_purchase_id must NOT have changed.
1486 +     async with shop.uow_factory() as uow:
1487 +         referral_after = await uow.referrals.get_by_referred(INVITED.telegram_id)
1488 +     assert referral_after is not None
1489 +     assert referral_after.discount_purchase_id == purchase_a.id
1490 +
1491 +
1492 + async def test_bug2_referral_reward_accrues_exactly_once(
1493 +     shop: Shop,
1494 + ) -> None:
1495 +     """The inviter earns the reward once, from the first completed purchase.
1496 +
1497 +     Settlement must not duplicate the reward entry. A second delivered purchase
1498 +     by the same invited buyer earns a separate reward for the inviter — but
1499 +     each purchase earns at most once (guaranteed by the unique constraint on
1500 +     ``(purchase_id, type)``).
1501 +     """
1502 +     await _buyers(shop, INVITER, INVITED)
1503 +     await _invite(shop, INVITER, INVITED)
1504 +
1505 +     before = await _balance(shop, INVITER.telegram_id)
1506 +
1507 +     # First purchase — discounted, earns reward.
1508 +     purchase = await _buy(shop, INVITED, await _product(shop, price_stars=1000))
1509 +     assert purchase.discount_amount == Decimal(100)
1510 +
1511 +     after_first = await _balance(shop, INVITER.telegram_id)
1512 +     reward = after_first - before
1513 +     assert reward > 0  # 15% of (1000 - 100) = 135
1514 +
1515 +     # Replayed settlement — must be idempotent, no extra reward.
1516 +     await shop.purchases.confirm_payment(
1517 +         provider=PaymentProvider.STARS,
1518 +         external_id=purchase.external_id,
1519 +     )
1520 +     assert await _balance(shop, INVITER.telegram_id) == after_first
1521 +
1522 +
1523 + async def test_bug1_concurrent_checkouts_serialised_by_for_update(
1524 +     shop: Shop,
1525 + ) -> None:
1526 +     """Bug #1: two truly concurrent checkouts on real PostgreSQL.
1527 +
1528 +     Both coroutines issue ``start_purchase`` for different products at the same
1529 +     moment.  The ``SELECT … FOR UPDATE`` on the referral row serialises them
1530 +     at the database level: one gets the lock first, creates a discounted pending
1531 +     purchase and commits; the other then gets the lock, re-checks, and sees
1532 +     the pending discount — so it creates a full-price purchase instead.
1533 +
1534 +     ``asyncio.gather`` is real concurrency here because the blocking happens
1535 +     inside ``asyncpg`` on the PostgreSQL wire, not on the Python event loop.
1536 +     """
1537 +     await _buyers(shop, INVITER, INVITED)
1538 +     await _invite(shop, INVITER, INVITED)
1539 +
1540 +     first_product = await _product(shop, price_stars=1000)
1541 +     second_product = await _product(shop, price_stars=1000)
1542 +
1543 +     async def checkout(product: Product) -> Purchase:
1544 +         return await shop.purchases.start_purchase(
1545 +             user_id=INVITED.telegram_id,
1546 +             product_id=product.id,
1547 +             provider=PaymentProvider.STARS,
1548 +             external_id=uuid4().hex,
1549 +         )
1550 +
1551 +     purchase_a, purchase_b = await asyncio.gather(
1552 +         checkout(first_product),
1553 +         checkout(second_product),
1554 +     )
1555 +
1556 +     # Both checkouts succeed (different products).
1557 +     assert purchase_a is not None
1558 +     assert purchase_b is not None
1559 +
1560 +     # Exactly one carries the discount.
1561 +     discounts = sorted(
1562 +         [purchase_a.discount_amount, purchase_b.discount_amount],
1563 +         reverse=True,
1564 +     )
1565 +     assert discounts == [Decimal(100), Decimal(0)], (
1566 +         f"Expected exactly one discount, got: "
1567 +         f"a={purchase_a.discount_amount}, b={purchase_b.discount_amount}"
1568 +     )
1569 +
1570 +
1571 + async def test_bug1_sequential_second_checkout_sees_pending_discount(
1572 +     shop: Shop,
1573 + ) -> None:
1574 +     """Bug #1 without concurrency: the second checkout for a different product
1575 +     sees the first pending discounted purchase and pays full price.
1576 +     """
1577 +     await _buyers(shop, INVITER, INVITED)
1578 +     await _invite(shop, INVITER, INVITED)
1579 +     product_a = await _product(shop, price_stars=1000)
1580 +     product_b = await _product(shop, price_stars=1000)
1581 +
1582 +     # First checkout — gets the discount.
1583 +     purchase_a = await shop.purchases.start_purchase(
1584 +         user_id=INVITED.telegram_id,
1585 +         product_id=product_a.id,
1586 +         provider=PaymentProvider.STARS,
1587 +         external_id=uuid4().hex,
1588 +     )
1589 +     assert purchase_a.discount_amount == Decimal(100)
1590 +     assert purchase_a.amount == Decimal(900)
1591 +
1592 +     # Second checkout — the pending discount guard blocks it.
1593 +     purchase_b = await shop.purchases.start_purchase(
1594 +         user_id=INVITED.telegram_id,
1595 +         product_id=product_b.id,
1596 +         provider=PaymentProvider.STARS,
1597 +         external_id=uuid4().hex,
1598 +     )
1599 +     assert purchase_b.discount_amount == Decimal(0)
1600 +     assert purchase_b.amount == Decimal(1000)
1601 +
1602 +
1603 + async def test_bug1_discount_becomes_available_again_after_pending_expires(
1604 +     shop: Shop,
1605 + ) -> None:
1606 +     """After the pending discounted purchase expires, the discount is available again.
1607 +
1608 +     The ``has_pending_discount`` guard must only block ``PENDING`` purchases,
1609 +     not expired ones.  Otherwise a buyer who abandoned a checkout would lose
1610 +     the discount permanently.
1611 +     """
1612 +     await _buyers(shop, INVITER, INVITED)
1613 +     await _invite(shop, INVITER, INVITED)
1614 +     abandoned = await _product(shop, price_stars=1000)
1615 +
1616 +     # Create a discounted pending purchase, then let it expire.
1617 +     purchase = await shop.purchases.start_purchase(
1618 +         user_id=INVITED.telegram_id,
1619 +         product_id=abandoned.id,
1620 +         provider=PaymentProvider.STARS,
1621 +         external_id=uuid4().hex,
1622 +     )
1623 +     assert purchase.discount_amount == Decimal(100)
1624 +
1625 +     await shop.purchases.expire_stale(now=_far_future())
1626 +
1627 +     # Now a fresh checkout should still get the discount.
1628 +     real = await _product(shop, price_stars=1000)
1629 +     real_purchase = await shop.purchases.start_purchase(
1630 +         user_id=INVITED.telegram_id,
1631 +         product_id=real.id,
1632 +         provider=PaymentProvider.STARS,
1633 +         external_id=uuid4().hex,
1634 +     )
1635 +     assert real_purchase.discount_amount == Decimal(100)

    - # --- The two pricing paths must agree
    - #
    - # There are two of them, and they run at different moments. ``quote_amount`` ->
    - # ``preview`` is read-only and runs *before* the purchase exists, because
    - # CryptoBot assigns the invoice id that later webhooks are matched on, so the
    - # invoice has to be raised first. ``start_purchase`` -> ``resolve`` then prices
    - # the sale authoritatively inside the transaction and refuses to record it at a
    - # number other than the one already invoiced.
    - #
    - # That refusal is a safety net, not a feature: whenever the two disagree the
    - # buyer simply cannot pay. So the agreement between them is the real contract,
    - # and this is the only place that holds them to it.
    -
    - STARS_PRICE = Decimal(1000)
    - CRYPTO_PRICE = Decimal("1.50")
    -

    -     ("currency", "price"),
    -     [(Currency.XTR, STARS_PRICE), (Currency.USDT, CRYPTO_PRICE)],
    -     ids=["stars", "crypto"],
    - )

1   + """The bonus service's guarantees about failing safely.
2   +
3   + The end-to-end file proves the feature works. This one proves the promises made
4   + about what happens when it does not: the master switch really disables
5   + everything, a courtesy message that cannot be delivered really is a non-event,
6   + and a ledger problem really cannot take a delivery down with it.
7   + """

40  + class BrokenNotifier:
41  +     """A transport that refuses both messages."""
42  +
43  +     async def notify_reward(self, notice: RewardNotice) -> None:
44  +         del notice
45  +         message = "chat unavailable"
46  +         raise RuntimeError(message)
47  +
48  +     async def notify_purchase_complete(self, user_id: int) -> None:
49  +         del user_id
50  +         message = "chat unavailable"
51  +         raise RuntimeError(message)
52  +
53  +
54  + class RecordingNotifier:
55  +     """Captures what would have been sent."""
56  +
57  +     def __init__(self) -> None:
58  +         self.rewards: list[RewardNotice] = []
59  +         self.hints: list[int] = []
60  +
61  +     async def notify_reward(self, notice: RewardNotice) -> None:
62  +         self.rewards.append(notice)
63  +
64  +     async def notify_purchase_complete(self, user_id: int) -> None:
65  +         self.hints.append(user_id)
66  +
67  +
68  + @pytest.fixture
69  + def unit() -> FakeUnitOfWork:
70  +     return FakeUnitOfWork()
71  +
72  +
73  + @pytest.fixture
74  + def uow_factory(unit: FakeUnitOfWork) -> FakeUnitOfWorkFactory:
75  +     return FakeUnitOfWorkFactory(unit)
76  +
77  +
78  + def _service(
79  +     uow_factory: FakeUnitOfWorkFactory,
80  +     *,
81  +     enabled: bool = True,
82  +     notifier: object | None = None,
83  + ) -> BonusService:
84  +     return BonusService(
85  +         uow_factory=uow_factory,
86  +         locks=FakeLockManager(),
87  +         settings=ReferralSettings(enabled=enabled),
88  +         notifier=notifier,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
89  +     )

348 +     assert offer.quote_with_bonus.charged_amount == Decimal(865)
349 +     assert offer.quote_without_bonus.charged_amount == Decimal(1000)

351 +
352 + # --- The two pricing paths must agree
353 + #
354 + # There are two of them, and they run at different moments. ``quote_amount`` ->
355 + # ``preview`` is read-only and runs *before* the purchase exists, because
356 + # CryptoBot assigns the invoice id that later webhooks are matched on, so the
357 + # invoice has to be raised first. ``start_purchase`` -> ``resolve`` then prices
358 + # the sale authoritatively inside the transaction and refuses to record it at a
359 + # number other than the one already invoiced.
360 + #
361 + # That refusal is a safety net, not a feature: whenever the two disagree the
362 + # buyer simply cannot pay. So the agreement between them is the real contract,
363 + # and this is the only place that holds them to it.
364 +
365 + STARS_PRICE = Decimal(1000)
366 + CRYPTO_PRICE = Decimal("1.50")
367 +
368 + RAILS = pytest.mark.parametrize(
369 +     ("currency", "price"),
370 +     [(Currency.XTR, STARS_PRICE), (Currency.USDT, CRYPTO_PRICE)],
371 +     ids=["stars", "crypto"],
372 + )
373 +
374 +
375 + async def _link(unit: FakeUnitOfWork, *, referrer: int, referred: int) -> None:
376 +     """An invited buyer who has not bought anything yet."""
377 +     await unit.users.upsert(UserDraft(telegram_id=referrer))
378 +     await unit.users.upsert(UserDraft(telegram_id=referred))
379 +     await unit.referrals.create(ReferralDraft(referrer_user_id=referrer, referred_user_id=referred))
380 +
381 +
382 + async def _grant(unit: FakeUnitOfWork, user_id: int, units: int) -> None:
383 +     await unit.users.upsert(UserDraft(telegram_id=user_id))
384 +     if units:
385 +         await unit.bonuses.add(
386 +             BonusTransactionDraft(
387 +                 user_id=user_id,
388 +                 amount=units,
389 +                 type=BonusTransactionType.REFERRAL_REWARD,
390 +             )
391 +         )
392 +

394 + @RAILS
395 + async def test_an_invited_buyers_first_purchase_previews_at_the_discounted_price(
396 +     uow_factory: FakeUnitOfWorkFactory,
397 +     unit: FakeUnitOfWork,
398 +     currency: Currency,
399 +     price: Decimal,
400 + ) -> None:
401 +     """The bug this test exists for, on the rail that had it.
402 +
403 +     ``offer_for`` used to return the *list* price for anything that was not
404 +     Stars, on the grounds that bonuses cannot be spent there. But the referral
405 +     discount is not a bonus — it is a percentage of the price, and it applies
406 +     to crypto too. So the card offered 1.35, the CryptoBot invoice was raised
407 +     for 1.50, and ``start_purchase`` refused the mismatch: every discounted
408 +     crypto checkout died with "не удалось создать счёт на оплату".
409 +     """
410 +     await _link(unit, referrer=INVITER, referred=INVITED)
411 +     service = _service(uow_factory)
412 +
413 +     previewed = await service.preview(
414 +         user_id=INVITED,
415 +         base_amount=price,
416 +         currency=currency,
417 +         use_bonus=False,
418 +     )
419 +
420 +     expected = Decimal(900) if currency is Currency.XTR else Decimal("1.35")
421 +     assert previewed.charged_amount == expected
422 +
423 +
424 + @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
425 + class Checkout:
426 +     """One situation a buyer can be in when they press a payment button."""
427 +
428 +     currency: Currency
429 +     price: Decimal
430 +     invited: bool
431 +     balance: int
432 +
433 +
434 + @pytest.mark.parametrize(
435 +     "case",
436 +     [
437 +         Checkout(currency=currency, price=price, invited=invited, balance=balance)
438 +         for currency, price in ((Currency.XTR, STARS_PRICE), (Currency.USDT, CRYPTO_PRICE))
439 +         for invited in (True, False)
440 +         for balance in (0, 300)
441 +     ],
442 +     ids=lambda case: (
443 +         f"{'stars' if case.currency is Currency.XTR else 'crypto'}"
444 +         f"-{'invited' if case.invited else 'ordinary'}"
445 +         f"-{'funded' if case.balance else 'broke'}"
446 +     ),
447 + )
448 + async def test_the_previewed_price_is_what_the_purchase_is_recorded_at(
449 +     uow_factory: FakeUnitOfWorkFactory,
450 +     unit: FakeUnitOfWork,
451 +     case: Checkout,
452 + ) -> None:
453 +     """Every situation the bot can actually reach, priced both ways.
454 +
455 +     ``use_bonus`` is derived the way the bot derives it — from the offer — so
456 +     this covers exactly the inputs production produces, and nothing that only a
457 +     hand-crafted callback could send.
458 +     """
459 +     if case.invited:
460 +         await _link(unit, referrer=INVITER, referred=INVITED)
461 +     await _grant(unit, INVITED, case.balance)
462 +     service = _service(uow_factory)
463 +
464 +     offer = await service.offer_for(
465 +         user_id=INVITED,
466 +         base_amount=case.price,
467 +         currency=case.currency,
468 +     )
469 +     use_bonus = offer.available
470 +
471 +     previewed = await service.preview(
472 +         user_id=INVITED,
473 +         base_amount=case.price,
474 +         currency=case.currency,
475 +         use_bonus=use_bonus,
476 +     )
477 +     resolved = await service.resolve(
478 +         unit,
479 +         user_id=INVITED,
480 +         base_amount=case.price,
481 +         currency=case.currency,
482 +         use_bonus=use_bonus,
483 +     )
484 +
485 +     assert previewed.charged_amount == resolved.charged_amount
486 +     assert previewed.discount_amount == resolved.discount_amount
487 +     assert previewed.bonus_units == resolved.bonus_units
488 +

37  + DELIVERY_URL = "https://t.me/+private-invite"

39  +
40  + def _settings(**overrides: object) -> DeliverySettings:
41  +     values: dict[str, object] = {
42  +         "max_attempts": 3,
43  +         "initial_backoff_seconds": 1.0,
44  +         "max_backoff_seconds": 10.0,
45  +         "backoff_multiplier": 2.0,
46  +         "jitter_ratio": 0.0,
47  +     }
48  +     values.update(overrides)
49  +     return DeliverySettings(**values)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
50  +
51  +
52  + class Harness:
53  +     """A wired PurchaseService + DeliveryService over in-memory doubles."""
54  +
55  +     def __init__(
56  +         self,
57  +         *,
58  +         failures: list[Exception] | None = None,
59  +         settings: DeliverySettings | None = None,
60  +     ) -> None:
61  +         self.uow_factory = FakeUnitOfWorkFactory()
62  +         self.locks = FakeLockManager()
63  +         self.gateway = FakeDeliveryGateway(failures)
64  +         self.sleeper = RecordingSleeper()
65  +         self.purchases = PurchaseService(uow_factory=self.uow_factory, locks=self.locks)
66  +         self.delivery = DeliveryService(
67  +             uow_factory=self.uow_factory,
68  +             purchases=self.purchases,
69  +             gateway=self.gateway,
70  +             locks=self.locks,
71  +             settings=settings or _settings(),
72  +             sleep=self.sleeper,
73  +             jitter=lambda: 0.5,
74  +         )
75  +
76  +     async def paid_purchase(self, *, provider: PaymentProvider = PaymentProvider.STARS) -> Purchase:
77  +         product = await self.uow_factory.unit.products.create(
78  +             ProductDraft(
79  +                 slug="vip1",
80  +                 title="VIP access",
81  +                 description="Access",
82  +                 delivery_url=DELIVERY_URL,
83  +                 price_stars=100,
84  +                 price_usdt=Decimal("4.99"),
85  +             )
86  +         )
87  +         await self.uow_factory.unit.users.upsert(BUYER)
88  +         await self.purchases.start_purchase(
89  +             user_id=BUYER.telegram_id,
90  +             product_id=product.id,
91  +             provider=provider,
92  +             external_id="inv-1",
93  +         )
94  +         return await self.purchases.confirm_payment(provider=provider, external_id="inv-1")

110 +     assert not message.is_repeat

115 +     assert harness.sleeper.delays == []

1   + """The rules that decide who is attributed to whom.
2   +
3   + Every case here is an abuse vector or a user mistake that the shop has to answer
4   + without breaking: inviting yourself, being invited twice, arriving as an
5   + existing buyer, or opening a link that no longer belongs to anybody.
6   + """
7   +

12  +

17  + from app.domain.enums import Currency, PaymentProvider, PurchaseStatus
18  + from app.domain.referrals import (
19  +     REFERRAL_PAYLOAD_PREFIX,

21  +     generate_referral_code,
22  +     is_referral_payload,
23  +     parse_referral_payload,
24  +     referral_payload,
25  + )
26  + from app.services.referrals import ReferralService
27  + from tests.fakes import FakeUnitOfWork, FakeUnitOfWorkFactory
28  + from tests.settings_factory import build_settings

31  +     from uuid import UUID

34  + INVITED = 2002

40  +     return FakeUnitOfWork()
41  +

58  + def _profile(telegram_id: int) -> UserDraft:
59  +     return UserDraft(telegram_id=telegram_id, username=f"user{telegram_id}")

62  + async def _code_of(service: ReferralService, telegram_id: int) -> str:
63  +     """Open the bonus screen, which is what mints a code."""
64  +     summary = await service.summary(_profile(telegram_id))
65  +     return summary.referral_code
66  +
67  +
68  + async def _record_purchase(
69  +     unit: FakeUnitOfWork,
70  +     telegram_id: int,
71  +     *,
72  +     status: PurchaseStatus = PurchaseStatus.DELIVERED,
73  + ) -> UUID:
74  +     product = await unit.products.create(
75  +         _product_draft(),
76  +     )
77  +     purchase = await unit.purchases.create(
78  +         PurchaseDraft(
79  +             user_id=telegram_id,
80  +             product_id=product.id,
81  +             provider=PaymentProvider.STARS,
82  +             amount=Decimal(1000),
83  +             currency=Currency.XTR,
84  +             external_id=f"invoice-{telegram_id}-{status.value}",
85  +             status=status,
86  +         )
87  +     )
88  +     return purchase.id

92  +     return ProductDraft(
93  +         slug=f"item{generate_referral_code()[:6]}",
94  +         title="VIP",
95  +         description="Access",
96  +         delivery_url="https://t.me/+private",
97  +         price_stars=1000,
98  +     )

104 + def test_a_referral_payload_is_recognised_by_its_prefix() -> None:
105 +     assert is_referral_payload(f"{REFERRAL_PAYLOAD_PREFIX}abcdef")
106 +     assert not is_referral_payload("muse")
107 +
108 +
109 + def test_a_code_round_trips_through_its_payload() -> None:
110 +     code = generate_referral_code()
111 +     assert parse_referral_payload(referral_payload(code)) == code
112 +
113 +
114 + def test_a_malformed_code_is_not_a_referral_payload() -> None:
115 +     """``None`` is what lets ``/start`` fall through to the product lookup.
116 +
117 +     A product whose slug happens to begin with "ref_" therefore keeps working,
118 +     which is why this returns ``None`` instead of raising.
119 +     """
120 +     assert parse_referral_payload("ref_") is None
121 +     assert parse_referral_payload("ref_UPPERCASE") is None
122 +     assert parse_referral_payload("ref_" + "a" * 40) is None
123 +     assert parse_referral_payload("muse") is None
124 +
125 +
126 + def test_a_generated_code_leaks_no_account_identifier() -> None:
127 +     """The code travels in a public link, so it must not encode the user.
128 +
129 +     Two codes minted in a row must differ, and neither may contain characters
130 +     that are routinely misread off a screen.
131 +     """
132 +     codes = {generate_referral_code() for _ in range(50)}
133 +     assert len(codes) == 50
134 +     assert all(not set(code) & set("ilo01") for code in codes)
